full_judgment:
Md Nuruzzaman J: The instant appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 27-6-2010 and 5-7-2010 respectively at the instance of the plaintiff passed by Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 264 of 2007 dismissing the suit.

2. The material facts relevant, for disposal of the instant First Appeal, succinctly, are that, the defendant No. 1 is the permanent citizen of Bangladesh and has been serving as Officer in the Arab Bangladesh Bank Limited. Moulana Mohammad, Salem Wahedi was his father who had been appointed as Nikah Registrar in the year of 1961. He had a good reputation as Marriage Registrar. The said Salem Wahedi purchased a property in the name of the defendant No. 1, as father vide registered deed No. 7416 of 1964 dated 11-8-1964 from the lease holder one Allahrakha Ansari who got the same from the government of erstwhile East Pakistan vide registered lease deed No. 5825 of 1963.

3. The defendant No. 1 Mohammad Obaidullah @ Obaidullah Aslam left the suit property at the time of liberation war due to abnormal situation at Mirpur Area. In the absence of defendant No. 1 some persons occupied the property and possessed the suit property collusively with the help of staff of the Deputy Commissioner Office. They treated the suit land as abandoned property vide Gazette notification dated 23-9-1986 which was published by the Ministry of Housing and Public Works. Thereafter, Mr Mohammad Obaidullah @ Obaidullah Aslam the defendant No. 1 made numerous applications to the concerned departments and authorities for exclusion of the suit property form "Ka" list but in vain. Thereafter, the defendant No. 1 Mr Obaidullah filed an application in the Court of Settlement, Segunbagicha, Dhaka which was registered as Settlement Case No. 55 of 1991. The aforementioned Settlement Case was heard by the Court of Settlement presiding over Mr Khandker Musa Khaled as chairman. The Court of settlement upon hearing both the sides by its Judgment dated 5-12-1995 excluded the suit property from the "Ka" list of abandoned building and further declared that the petitioner is entitled to return back the possession of the house immediately.

4. The defendant No. 1 Mr Mohammad Obaidullah @ Obaidullah Aslam on 23-1-2006 executed and registered an irrevocable Power of Attorney in favour of Alhaj MNA Afgani to do all the necessary works regarding the suit property on his behalf. Mr Mohammad Obaidullah @ Obaidullah Aslam on 4-5-2006 through legally constituted attorney executed a sale deed of agreement for sale of the suit property in favour of Mrs Mosammat Amena Begum receiving Taka 7,00,000 (Seven lac) out of total consideration money of Taka 7,50,000 (Seven lac fifty thousand).

5. The deed of agreement for sale was registered on 4-6-2006 being deed No. 3432. On 1-4-2007 Mr Mohammad Obaidullah Salim through attorney receipt Taka 30,000 (Thirty Thousand) out of rest of consideration money Taka 50,000 (Fifty thousand) and handed over the possession of the suit property to the plaintiff Musammat Amena Begum in presence of witnesses on promise to register the deed of sale either himself or through his Attorney very soon on receipt of balance of Taka 20,000 (Twenty thousand).

6. The purchaser due to delay the registration of the sale deed took over the possession of the suit property from DNA holder occupant Md. Hafizur Rahman and obtained a written deed from attorney Alhaj MNA Afgani and she also got the delivery of possession of all the original documents. The plaintiff according to the deed of agreement of sale offer the balance money of Taka 20,000 (Twenty thousand) on 29/30 Oct 2007 to the Attorney of defendant No. 1 and requested him to execute and register the deed of sale in favour of the plaintiff. However, Mr MNA Afgani the attorney of the vendor took dilatory tactic on the various pretend and said that he would execute and register the sale deed after some days. The plaintiff when ask him to fix a specific day but he declined to say the fix date of registration, not any that all on a sudden at the time of conversation he told that he will not execute and register the sale deed. Due to such activities of the Attorney of defendant No. 1 the plaintiff has not been able to register the deed of sale. In the meantime the plaintiff came to learn on a reliable source that the defendant No. 1 and his Attorney for illegal gain most illegally trying to sell the suit property to the other person depriving the plaintiff from his legal and legitimate claim and right. The plaintiff while residing in the suit property some purchaser had come to see the house to purchase the property. In such facts and circumstances the plaintiffs was in serious doubt that she would be ousted and further more sufferer due to illegal steps of the defendant No. 1 and his Attorney. The plaintiff having no other alternative but has been compelled to file the suit for Specific Performance of Contract and permanent injunction against the defendants.

7. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the statement made in paragraph 1 to 8 are matter of records and the plaintiff is put to strict prove of the case however, they have believed that the value of the suit property is more then 7,50,000 (Seven Lac and fifty thousand) as it was decided on 4-5-2006 through registered deed of agreement however, in the facts of the case of the written statement the Attorney of the defendant No. 1 himself admit the facts of contract for sale. But he claimed Taka 1,00,000 (One lac) extra for increasing the value of the suit with rest Taka 20,000 (Twenty thousand) in total 1,20,000 (One lac and twenty thousand) for execution and registration of the sale deed within 2/3 months.

8. The learned Joint District on perusal of the pleadings of both the sides framed the following issues:

1) Whether the suit is maintainable in its present form and manner ?

2) Whether the claim of the plaintiff is correct or not ?

3) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to get the relief as prayed for ?

9. The plaintiff to prove his plaint case examined 4 witnesses. PW 1 AKM Hafizur Rahman, PW 2 Haji Hossen, PW 3 Bodiuzzaman, PW 4 Md Nurul Amin. The plaintiff side to prove the case also produced some documentary evidences which have been marked as exhibits. Power-of-Attorney dated 10-9-2009 is exhibit 1. Judgment of Settlement case No. 55 of 1991 is exhibit 2. Deed No. 7416 dated 11-8-1964 is exhibit 3, lease deed No. 5825 dated 16-4-1963 is exhibit 4, deed of agreement for sale dated 4-6-2006 is exhibit 5 and 5(1), the deed of agreement for possession and receipt of Taka exhibit 6, the deed of possession handed over to the plaintiff is exhibit 7, Death Certificate dated 12-4-1954 is exhibit 8, citizen certificate in the name of Md Obaidullah is exhibit-9, letter of possession in favour of Allahrakha is exhibit 10, Death Certificate of Allahrakha Ansari is exhibit 11.

10. On the other hand, the defendant to substantiate the defence case as narrated in the written statement examined 2 witnesses. DW 1 MNA Afgani, DW 2 Advocate Chowdhury Wahidur Rahman. The defendants side also produced some documentary evidences which have been marked as exhibits. exhibit 'Ka' Power of Attorney dated 23-1-2006, Exhibit-'Kha' Letter of Administrative officer vide No. 745 dated 27-7-1964, Exhibit 'Ga' to 'Ga(14)' Bill of Dhaka Electic Supply, Exhibit 'Gha', Gha (1)' and 'Gha(2)' Certificate upon Form-A, exhibit 'Uma' and 'Uma(1)' Notices of Case No. 55 of 1991 dated 1-10-1991, exhibit 'Cha' Voter list, Exhibit 'Chaa' Letter dated 29-3-1978 exhibit Jo Letter dated 5-7-1978.

11. The learned Joint District Judge, Arbitration Adalat by his Judgment and decree dated 27-6-2010 and 5-7-2010 respectively passed in Title Suit No. 264 of 2007 dismissing the suit on contest against the defendant No. 1 and ex-parte against the rest defendants.

12. The plaintiff feeling aggrieved by the Judgment and decree dated 27-6-2010 and 5-7-201 respectively passed in Title Suit No. 264 of 2007 preferred the instant First Appeal before this Court.

13. At first we shall meticulously examine the testimonies of all the PWs and DWs. Thereafter, we shall discussed the legality and propriority of the documentary evidences to come on a definite findings.

14. Mr AKM Hafizur Rahman PW 1 has testified that he is husband and Attorney of the plaintiff. He has produced the Power of Attorney which is exhibit 1. The defendant No. 1 is the owner of the suit land and suit was filed for specific performance of contract and permanent injunction. The defendant No. 1 is a permanent citizen of Bangladesh by birth who has been serving in the Arab Bangladesh Bank Limited as an Officer. He is the son of Moulana Mohammad Salem Wahedi who was the Nikah Registrar of Sutrapur area. He was appointed in the year of 1961 and working till day. He knows the sister and brother of the defendant and they are elite of the society. In the year of 1948 while defendant No. 1 was minor his father Kazi Saheb purchased the suit land through registered sale deed in the name of defendant No. 1. The said deed has been lying with him. Allahrakha Ansari got the lease from the government. Allahrakha Ansari obtained the income tax clearance and transferred the same to the defendant No. 1. The Original lease deed was in the name of the Allahrakha Ansari, the government handed over the possession to Allahrakha Ansari.

15. The defendant No. 1 has been owning and possessing the suit property. The defendant No. 1 left the suit property during the liberation war for unavoidable situation therefore, the suit property becomes the abandoned property. The defendant No. 1 time and again filed the applications for recovery of the suit property. Thereafter, the defendant No. 1 filed a case to the Court of Settlement for exclusion of the suit property and obtained order in his favour. In this way, the suit property was released from the list of the abandoned property. There was a order to hand over the possession of the property. He got the Judgment of the Court of Settlement in his favour and there is a settlement in respect of papers and case of the Court of Settlement.

16. The government did not file any appeal against the judgment of the Court of settlement therefore; the Judgment of the Court of settlement becomes absolute. On 23-1-2006 the defendant No. 1 appointed Mr MNA Afgani as Attorney to look after the property and do others necessary work. The said Power of Attorney was registered in. the Mirpur Sub-Registrar Office. The Power of Attorney on 4-5-2006 made an agreement for sale which was executed and registered on the same day fixing the value of the property Taka 7,50,000 (Seven lac fifty thousand) out of which the Attorney received Taka 7,00,000 (Seven lac). The deed of agreement being No. 3432 dated 4-6-2006 is lying with plaintiff No. 1.

17. On 28-2-2007 the defendant No. 1 through Attorney had given the letter of Apush Nama (আপোষনামা) to the plaintiff receiving Taka 30,000 (Thirty thousand) out of rest Taka 50,000 (Fifty thousand). There is a letter of Acknowledgement. There was a settlement to register the sale deed within 13-10-2007. He has submitted the certified copy of the Judgment of settlement Court dated 5-12-1995 passed in Settlement Case No. 55 of 1991. He has submitted the original deed being No. 7416 dated 11-8-1963 exhibit 3, exhibit 4 is the original lease deed being No. 5825 dated 16-4-1963 in the name of Allahrakh Ansari. The deed of Baina Nama dated 4-5-2006 being No. 3432 exhibit 5 (with objection). exhibit 6 is the letter of possession dated 1-4-2007, exhibit 7 is the letter of possession dated 28-2-2007, exhibit 8 is the birth certificate of defendant No.1. He has submitted the photocopy of the appointment letter of the father of defendant No. 1, exhibit 9 is the original citizen certificate issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs with forwarding letter. He requested the Attorney of defendant No. 1 to execute and register the sale deed. He was ready to pay the rest of Taka 20,000 and till now he is ready to pay the said money. The defendant No. 1 and his attorney trying to sold out the suit property to other persons. Some buyer came in the suit property to see it. The Attorney has no right to sell the property to other person. He has submitted the document of possession dated 3-7-1963 which is exhibit 10. Exhibit 11 is the certified copy of the death certificate of Allahrakha Ansari. Not a fact that there was talk to pay of Taka 1,20,000 (One lac twenty thousand) and if he paid the same then deed will execute. He prayed for decree for specific performance of contract on behalf of defendant No. 1.

18. In cross: PW 1 replied that he was a government servant now he is in retirement. Not a fact that there was a conversation to pay Taka 1,00,000 (One lac) in addition of consideration money. Not a fact that the story of sell of the of the suit property to other person is false. Not a fact that if pay additional Taka 1,00,000 (One lac) instead of filing the suit, then he would have the deed.

19. PW 2 Hazi Hossain. He knows the plaintiff and defendants. The suit plot is house No. 6-D, 5/18. Deed of agreement for sale was made on 4-5-2006 between the parties. He was the witness to the Bainanama dated 4-5-2006. He has signed in the Bainanama. This is his signature exhibit 5/1. At the time of registration of the Bainanama Taka 7,00,000 (Seven lac) was paid by the plaintiff.

20. In cross he replied that he has come in the Court on receiving the summon. He did not know whether after the Baina Nama there was a discussion among the parties regarding the financial matters.

21. PW 3 Bodiuzzaman. He knows the plaintiff and defendant. On 4-5-2006 he has signed in the Baina Patra being No. 3432 and his signature in the Baina Patra is exhibit 5(2). He is the scribe. The deed of agreement was written in his office. The price was Taka 7,50,000 out of consideration money 700,000 (Seven lac) has been paid.

22. In cross: he replied that he sit in the sub-registered office at Mirpur. He has come to the Court today on receiving the summon. He did not know about the financial transaction after the Bainanama.

23. PW 4 Md Nurul Amin. He knows the plaintiff and defendant. In his presence on 1-4-2007 the defendant handed over the possession of the suit property to the plaintiff. He has signed in the deed of possession as witness. The plaintiff in his presence paid Taka 30,000 (Thirty thousand) to the defendant.

24. In cross he replied that he did not know whether there is a conversation on behalf of the defendant to pay Taka 1,00,000 (One lac) in addition of remaining money 20,000 (Twenty thousand). It was stipulated that the rest of the money would be paid at the time of handing over the possession. Not a fact that he did not know about the payment of the plaintiff. Not a fact that he has testified falsely.

25. DW 1 MNA Afgani. He testified that he is the Attorney of defendant No. 1. Allahrakha Ansari was the original owner of the suit property. Allahrakha Ansari got the suit property on 16-4-1963 vide deed No. 5825. On 11-8-1964 Allahrakha Ansari transferred the suit property to the defendant No. 1 vide deed being No. 7416. Allahrakha Ansari has paid the government dues. The suit property was purchased in the name of defendant No. 1 by his father. At the time of liberation war in 1971 the defendant No. 1 resided in the suit property. Due to fear of life he left the resident and went to Kalotola, Sutrapur (কলুটোলা, সূত্রাপুর)।After liberation he went to the suit property and saw some trespassers possessed the property. They had listed the suit property as an abandoned property. After liberation the father of defendant No. 1 made numerous applications to the government for release of the suit property but all were in vain. Thereafter, he un-successfully filed the case being Settlement Case No. 55 of 1991 in the Court of Settlement Court No. I. On 5-12-1995 the Court of Settlement passed the Judgment and order excluding the suit property from the list of abandoned property and directed the government to hand over the possession of the suit property to the defendant No. 1. The government did not file any appeal or writ against the said Judgment of the Court of Settlement. The defendant No. 1 made a registered Power of Attorney being No. 381 in, his name. The Attorney on behalf of the defendant No. 1 made a registered Bainapatra on 4-5-2006 receiving Taka 7,00,000 (Seven lac) out of total consideration of Taka 7,50,000 (Seven lac and fifty thousand). On 8-2-2007 he got possession of the suit property. On 1-4-2007 he handed over the possession to the plaintiff. In the same day he got Taka 30,000 (Thirty thousand) from the plaintiff out of remaining Taka 50,000 (Fifty thousand). He has claimed Taka 1,00,000 (One lac) more for register of the suit property at the ending of October 2007. At the instance of defendant No. 1 the plaintiff was agreed to pay the said money. He demand Taka 1,20,000 (One lac and twenty thousand) however, the plaintiff filed the suit without payment of Taka 1,20,00 (One lac and twenty thousand). The plaintiff if paid Taka 1,20,000 (One lac and twenty thousand) he would have registered the deed in that case there would be no cause of action for filing the suit. The plaintiff filed the suit due to misunderstanding and there is no cause of action to file the suit. The defendant No. 1 now has been serving Arab Bangladesh Bank under Bongshal Branch. He prays for dismissal of the suit. He submitted the Power of Attorney dated 23-1-2006 being No. 381 which has been marked as exhibit 'Ka'. He has produced the letter being No. 745 dated 27-7-1964 which has been marked as exhibit 'Kha'. He has produced electricity bill of 15 pieces which has been marked exhibit 'Ga'. He has filed the certificate in form-A which has been marked as exhibit 'Gha'. He has produced the 2nd notice of the Case No. 55 of 1991 which has been marked as exhibit 'Uma'. He has produced 01 copy of notice which has been marked as exhibit 'Cha'. He has produced the letter vide memo No. AB-282/75 I 229(1) dated 29-3-1978 which has been marked exhibit 'Chha (ছ)'. He has produced the letter dated 5-7-1978 being memo No. 93 (নি-২) which has been marked as exhibit la(w)'.

26. In cross he replied that the signature of the defendant No. 1 has identified by Advocate Chowdhury Wahidur Rahman. He has given the documents to the plaintiffs. Allahrakha Ansari died on 2-6-1967. Not a fact that demand of additional Taka 1,00,000 (One lac) is illegal. Not a fact that he has deposed falsely.

27. DW 2 Chowdhury Wahidur Rahman Advocate. He has stated that the draft of Power of Attorney made by him. He has identified the signature of defendant No. 1. The defendant No. 1 has signed in his presence. He has signed in the page No. 8 of the power of attorney which has been marked exhibit Ka(1). He has signed in the Power of Attorney No. 381 as identifier and he has signed in the Power of Attorney which has been marked exhibit-Ka(2). No Cross.

28. Mr Deb Das Sammaddar has submitted that the plaintiff produced all the documentary evidences to prove the plaint case including the deed of agreement for sale as well as registered Power of Attorney. Mr Sammaddar has further submitted that the trial Court misread and misconstrued the evidences on record thereby failed to consider all the exhibits in its true perspective. He has added that not only that the Court below misread the exhibit '2' in not considering the same as certified copy of Court of Settlement and, as such, judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside. He has further added that the suit is for specific performance of contract and permanent injunction wherein the plaintiff was able to prove the transaction of Bainanama including handing over the possession of the suit property and original deed of vendor. So, the learned Judge erred in law in dismissing the suit. In support of his submission he cited some precedence's which are to the case of the People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Public Works vs The Chairman, Court of Settlement reported in 17 BLD (AD) 301 = 50 DLR (AD) 93, to the case of Nitai Ch. Shaha vs M/s City Ice and Cold Storage Ltd reported in 35 DLR 60, to the case of Nurul Islam vs Jamila Khatun reported in 53 DLR (AD) 45, to the case of Akbar Hossain (Md) vs Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Housing and Works reported 48 DLR 191.

29. We have gone through the plaint, written statement all the testimonies of PWs and DWs and documentary evidences produced by PW 1. Exhibit '1' is the Power of Attorney affirmed before the Notary Public on 10-9-2009. Exhibit '2' the Judgment of the Court of Settlement passed in Case No. 55 of 1991 (Ka 236 Mirpur, Dhaka), the deed dated 11 August 1964 exhibit '3'. The Sketch map exhibit '4', deed of agreement for sale dated 4th May 2006 executed by MNA Afgani on behalf of his principle Md Obaidullah Salem in favour of Mrs Amena Begum wife of AKM Hafizur Rahman exhibit '5', exhibit '6' is deed of handing over the possession of the property and money receipt dated 1-4-2007, exhibit '7' is the deed of handing over the possession by one Hafizur Rahman in favour of Md Obaidullah Saleh alias Aslam, exhibit '8' is the Birth Certificate fathers name of Salim dated29 December 1997, exhibit '9' is the application to the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs dated 8-3-1978, exhibit '10' is the letter vide memo No. 2905 dated 5-6-1963, exhibit '11' is the death certificate of Allahrakha Ansari dated 5-7-1983.

30. On sifting the oral evidences of PWs it appear that PW 1 AKM Hafizur Rahman, son of Unus Mia of House No. 18, Road No. 5, Block D, Mirpur Section 6 Dhaka. One perusal of the Power of Attorney exhibit 1 it appears that the said PW is none but the husband of the plaintiff. who also made the deed of agreement of possession handing over the suit property to his wife stating his name as Md Hafizur Rahman however, the present address and father name and permanent address given in the exhibit '8' and address of others documentary evidences i.e. exhibit '7', '6' and exhibit '1' are the same. So, it is proved through documentary evidences that the handing over of possession of the suit property to the plaintiff not by the government but PW 1 who is none but her husband. On cross-examination he admitted that he was a government officer however, he has concealed the facts that he was a DNA holder of the government and in connivance with the defendant No. 1 prepared a Power of Attorney. Thereafter, through Power of Attorney he made a deed of agreement for sale of the suit property in the name none but his wife, therefore, we have no hesitation to opine that the PW 1 has made the document i.e. sale of agreement and agreement of handing over the possession of the suit property with connivance in favour of his wife to grab same.

31. But facts remains that through exhibit '2'. Judgment of the Settlement Court they never got possession from the government. The ownership of the original owner was not denied by the government but admittedly the property was listed in the "Ka" list, of the abandoned property which proved that the defendant No. 1 was/is not possessed in the suit property. So, we find that the suit property was never possessed by the defendant No. 1. More so, it appears from the record that deed of agreement for sale registered on 4-5-2006 and filing of the suit on 29-11-2007.

<u>32. Therefore, it is crystal clear that the instant suit was instituted long after 1 year. According to the last amendment of Article 113 of the Limitation Act made in the year 2004 limitation for filing the suit for Specific Performance of Contract is 1 (one) year from the date of execution and registration of the deed of sale agreement.</u>

<u>33. Furthermore, the provision of section 21A of the Specific Relief Act speaks the suit for Specific Performance of Contract must be instituted by depositing the balance amount of consideration money in the Court at the time of filing of the suit, otherwise, the suit would not be registered but if so registered and proceeded that would be flagrant violation of the provision of section 21A of the Registration Act.</u>

34. For the ready reference and convenience of the discussions we may reproduced the provision of section 21A Specific Relief Act and Article 113 of the Limitation Act which runs as follows:

21A. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Act or any other law for the time being in force, no contract for sale of any immovable property can be specifically enforced unless—

(a)	the contract is in writing and registered under the Registration Act, 1908, whether or not the transferee has taken possession of the property or any part thereof; and

(b)	the balance amount of consideration of the contract is deposited in the court at the time of tiling the suit for specific performance of the contract.

(c)	Of the discretion of the Court. Article 113 of the Limitation Act:

113.	For specific performance of a contract

1[One year]

The date fixed for the performance, or, if no such date is fixed, when the plaintiff has notice that performance is refused.

<u>35. On perusal of the provision as quoted herein above we find that the suit was filed after expiry of the limitation and in violation of section 21A of the Specific Relief Act. It has been provided in the provision of section 21A the balance amount of consideration must be deposited at the time of filing of the suit which is mandatory therefore, we find that the suit has been filed in violation of the above law and, as such, the suit is not maintainable and the plaintiff is not entitled to have the decree for Specific Performance of Contract.</u>

36. More so, from the Judgment of the Court below it appears that the learned Judge after consideration of the documentary evidence came to the conclusion that the handing over the possession and preparation of the documents is anything but concocted papers. We find that the preparation and registration of Bainanama by dint of Power of Attorney is not proved because neither the principal was examined to prove the Power of Attorney nor the Power of Attorney in original was produced in Court. So, the power of attorney has not been marked as exhibit to proof the genuineness of it in accordance with law. We are, therefore, of the considered view that the plaintiff has failed to prove the basis of the Bainanama in accordance with law. It is our further opinion that there is no legal and lawful error nor the Judgment and decree passed by the Court below is tainted or suffers from legal infirmity which does not call any interferences by this Court.

<u>37. More so, passing a decree in a suit for Specific Performance of Contract is a discretionary relief at the discretion of the Court, to have the such relief the plaintiff must come with clean hand but from the events of the case it is apparent that the plaintiff, the defendant No. 1 and his so called attorney did not make the agreement for sale in clean hand. The plaintiff rather, has created the agreement for purchase of the property who is not in possession of the same and thereafter she played a highly unpleasant events in the name of taking over the possession of the suit property in connivance with her husband which proved that the agreement for sale following transaction as consideration is nothing but a concocted and fabricated events only to grab the property abusing the process of the court in the name of Specific Performance of Contract through an agreement for sale.</u>

38. The pertinent question is whether DNA holder cans handover the possession of the abandoned property to a party who is none but his wife who make a contract for purchase the property or the DNA holder under obligation to handover the possession of the property to the Government?

39. We are of the considered view that the status of a DNA holder is nothing more than a allottee from the authorise person of the Government not a tenant or representative of original owner. We are therefore of the opinion that such allottee has no locus-standi to hand-over the possession of an abandoned property to a third party who make a contract to a party claiming the ownership who had/has never in possession of the property. Any DNA holder if make any such nature of handing over of possession of a abandoned property it would be surely treated as serious violation of the stipulation of the allotment of DNA holder as the DNA holder having no right, title or possession as a matter of personal individual but allottee of the government such handing over of possession must be treated as honest in the eye of law.

<u>40. The precedence’s referred by the learned Advocate for the appellant on perusal the same it appear that the facts and circumstances of these cases are quite distinguishable from the facts of the case in hand. Therefore, although we are not disagreeing with those principles, however, we are unable to accept and make those applicable in the present case.</u>

41. Thus, the appeal having no merit, it fails.

42. Accordingly, the appeal is disallowed however, without any order as to cost.

Office is directed to communicate the Judgment to the trial Court and send down the lower Court's record at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Mahmudul Hoque, J.: In this revision Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-7 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 17.05.2015 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong in Other Appeal No. 228 of 2009 disallowing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 29.06.2009 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sitakunda, Sadar, Chittagong in Other Suit No. 16 of 2001 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioner, as plaintiff, instituted Other Suit No. 16 of 2001 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Sitakunda, Sadar, Chittagong, against the opposite party, as defendant, for declaration of title in the schedule 1 (Ka) property to the plaint stating inter alia that the defendant No. 6 Nur Khatun was the owner of the property under R.S. plot Nos. 4767 and 4778 by purchase from Ayesha Khatun and Aminul Huq by registered deed No. 579 dated 25.02.1972 and registered deed No. 2371 dated 10.12.1979. The defendant No. 6 also purchased 24 sataks of land under R.S. plot Nos. 4981 and 4982 from one Nurul Huq by a registered deed No. 2083 dated 26.04.1976. While she was in possession of the property by purchase, mortgaged the property under R.S. plot Nos. 4981 and 4982 to one Saera Khatun by a registered deed of mortgage dated 10.12.1969 which was subsequently redeemed by herby a registered deed of reconveyance No. 1443. Said Nur Khatun while in possession and enjoyment of the property executed a bainanama in favour of plaintiff on 02.03.1998. Following the said bainanama, Nur Khatun executed and registered a sale deed on 09.03.1999 in favour of the plaintiff and delivered all the original documents relating to the property. Later on, some of the original documents were stolen from the house of the plaintiff for which he lodged a diary in the court of 1st Class Magistrate. After purchase, the plaintiff got his name mutated in B.S. khatian No. 3179 by Mutation Case No. 20/1999-2000 and paid rent to the government. Since then the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land with the knowledge of defendants. On 20.01.2001 the defendant No. 1 tried to interfere with the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land and denied the title of the plaintiff. Thereafter, the plaintiff received a notice from the Assistant Commissioner Land "AC (Land)" on 01.02.2001 and came to know that the defendant No. 1 filed an objection against the Mutation Case No.20/1999-2000. The plaintiff appeared before the AC (Land) on 11.02.2001 and submitted all the relevant documents before him who after hearing the parties most illegally cancelled the mutation in the name of the plaintiff. The decision cancelling mutation of the plaintiff by AC (Land) is illegal, void and inoperative. For claiming title over the property by defendant No. 1 and cancellation of the mutation in the name of the plaintiff, the plaintiff's title have become clouded. Hence, the present suit for declaration of title and for declaration that the order cancelling mutation of the plaintiff by AC (Land) is illegal and without jurisdiction.

3. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint, contending inter alia, that the defendant No. 6, Nur Khatun acquired title and possession in 10 sataks land appertaining to R.S. plot Nos. 4767 and 4778 by purchase from Ayesha KhatlIn by registered deed No. 579 dated 29.02.1972. Said Ayesha Khatun also sold 20 sataks of land to Aminul Huq husband of Nur Khatun by registered kabala No. 578 dated 29.02.1972 and delivered possession of the same to them. Thereafter, Aminul Haque again transferred the said 20 sataks of land to his wife Nur Khatun by a registered deed No. 5329 dated 10.12.1979 and delivered possession of the same. Since then Nur Khatun had been in possession by purchase on payment of rent to the government. One Mariam Bibi having title over 5 sataks land in R.S. plot Nos. 4767 and 4778, sold it out to the defendant No. 1 by a registered sale deed No. 1124 dated 03.04.1962 who purchased the same in the benami of his father. Thereafter, Nur Khatun proposed to sell the land measuring 4 sataks appertaining to R.S plot Nos. 4767 and 4778 at a consideration of Tk. 4,000/- to defendant No. 1 and the defendant No. 1 purchased the same by registered kabala No. 2733 dated 11.06.1982: Subsequently, said Nur Khatun offered to sell 7 sataks of land under R.S. plot Nos. 4767 and 4778 to defendant No. 1 at a consideration of Tk. 10,000/-. But before drafting and execution of the sale deed, the defendant No. 1 came to know that Nur Khatun had gifted 3 sataks of land to her daughter Samuda Khatun.

4. In such a situation, the defendant No. 1 decided to get the deed from both Nur Khatun and Samuda Khatun. Consequently, the defendant No. 1 purchased the land measuring 7 sataks from Nur Khatun and Samuda Khatun by a registered deed No. 3008 dated 25.05.1983 and got possession of the same in line with the property purchased earlier from Nur Khatun. In the way aforesaid the defendant No. 1 acquired title and possession in 11 sataks of land and have been possessing the same with the knowledge of the plaintiff upon payment of rent to the government. In addition to the transaction mentioned above, Nur Khatun sold out the remaining 23 sataks land in R.S. plot Nos. 4767 and 4778 to the defendant No. 1 by a registered deed No. 1087 dated 05.04.1999 and in the said deed one Md. Iqbal Hossain son of plaintiff Shamsul Alam was an attesting witness. It is further stated that Nur Khatun executed all the sale deeds in favour of defendant No. 1 and others by putting her thumb impression as she was an illiterate women. While the plaintiff at the back of the defendant No. 1 got his name mutated in the relevant khatian in Mutation Case No. 20/1999-2000, the defendant No. 1 filed an objection before the AC (Land) in which notice was duly served upon the plaintiff, who appeared in the objection case and after hearing both the parties AC (land) cancelled the mutation in the name of the plaintiff and mutated the name of the defendant No. 1 by a Mutation Case No. 24/2000-2001.

5. The sale deed in question by which the plaintiff claims the property by purchase from Nur Khatun is false, forged and fabricated one and has been created by the plaintiff only to grab the property of the defendant No. 1, as such, the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed.

6. The trial court framed five issues for determination of the dispute. In course of hearing the plaintiff examined three witnesses as P.Ws. and the defendant No.1 examined four witnesses as D.Ws. Both the parties submitted certain documents in support of their claim which were duly marked as exhibits. The trial court upon hearing dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 29.06.2009.

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court, the plaintiff preferred Other Appeal No. 228 of 2009 which was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, Court, Chittagong, on transfer who upon hearing disallowed the appeal by the impugned judgment and decree. At this juncture, the petitioner moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of status quo.

8. The opposite party No. 1 contested the Rule by filing counter affidavit and supplementary affidavit.

9. Mr. Anwarul Azim Khayer with Mr. Mohammad Nurul Huda Ansary learned Advocates appearing for the petitioner submit that the plaintiff-petitioner purchased the suit property from Nur Khatun by virtue of an agreement for sale dated 02.03.1999 and following the said agreement Nur Khatun executed sale deed on 09.03.1999, and the deed of defendant No. 1 was executed on 09.04.1999. As such, the deed of the plaintiff is earlier one in point of time and the same has precedence over the document of the defendant No. 1 under section 47 of the Registration Act, but the appellate court most unfortunately failed to consider such provisions of law. In support of his such submissions he has referred to the case of Mir Abdul Ali Vs. Md. Rafiqul Islam Khan reported in 40 DLR (AD) 75.

10. He further submits that defendant No. 6 Nur Khatun appeared in the suit and filed written statement admitting execution and registration of the deed in favour of the plaintiff and denying execution of any deed and registration of the same in favour of the defendant No. 1. But said Nur Khatun did not come before the court to depose and to support her such contention and the parties to the proceedings also did not cite her as witness on their behalf. Since Nur Khatun is still alive, her evidence for proper adjudication of the matter in dispute and to ensure justice between the parties is required to be recorded as to whether she executed any deed of sale in favour of the plaintiff or in favour of the defendant No. 1. As such, he prays for sending the case on remand for recording evidence of Nur Khatun only. In support of his such submissions he has referred to the case of Shawkat Hossain (Md) and another vs. Golam Mohammad and another reported in 20 BLC (AD) 27.

11. Mr. Azim further submits that the defendant No. I did not cross examine or give any suggestion to P.W. 1 while he was cross examining, to the effect that Nur Khatun did not file any written statement in the suit or the written statement as lying in the record has been filed by the plaintiff by forging her signature or otherwise. Where the written statement filed by defendant No. 6 has not been challenged or any suggestions made on behalf of the defendant No. 1 the written statement should be considered as genuine one and the contents therein to be considered as true, but both the courts below overlooked the written statement filed by the defendant No. 6, Nur Khatun. It is also argued that had it been considered by both the courts below it would find that Nur Khatun admittedly executed sale deed in favour of the plaintiff and delivered possession of the same to him.

12. Mr. Lokman Karim, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1 at the very outset submits that admittedly, the property in question originally belonged to Nur Khatun by purchase, who transferred a portion of the property along with her daughter to the defendant No. 1 by deed No. 2733 dated 11.06.1982 (exhibit-ঠ) and deed No. 3008 dated 22.2.1983 (exhibit-ড) and those deeds have not been challenged by the plaintiff, rather the plaintiff unequivocally admitted the existence of those deeds which were executed by Nur Khatun putting her thumb impression.

13. He further submits that said Nur Khatun executed and registered a deed of mortgage dated 10.12.1969 (exhibit-5) filed by the plaintiff, also executed by putting her thumb impression. But the deed of the plaintiff dated 09.03.1999 is appearing to have been executed by Nur Khatun putting her signature who is an illiterate women. He further submits that the plaintiff in his cross examination firmly asserted that he will produce said Nur Khatun before the court to depose in respect of the sale deed dated 09.03.1999. But ultimately Nur Khatun was not examined by the plaintiff to prove that she executed the sale deed by putting her signature in favour of the plaintiff. As such, the courts below rightly held and observed that the plaintiff utterly failed to prove the sale deed and agreement for sale (exhibits-8 and 11) by any reliable evidence. He further submits that no attesting witness to the deed has been examined by the plaintiff to prove execution of the deed in question by Nur Khtun. But examined, only the scriber as P.W. 3 who in his cross examination clearly stated that the stamp on which he has written the deed was purchased in the name of plaintiff and the sale deed submitted in the court containing sanad number is not of him. The plaintiff also stated that the bainanama in which Nur Khatun put her signature was written by deed writer, but the bainanama itself shows that it is a typed one. It is also submitted that the deed writer stated that the stamp was purchased by plaintiff, but the plaintiff himself stated that the stamp was purchased by the deed writer.

14. Mr. Karim further submits that the stamps are usually to be purchased in the name of purchaser or may be in the name of the seller. But the stamp on which the deed dated 09.03.1999 has been written are in the name of one Ziaul Haque of Chunoti, Lohagora, but the purchaser plaintiff is a man of Sitakunda. Moreover, in the deed the said Ziaul Haque in whose name stamp was purchased not an attesting witness. He further submits that Nur Katun executed another sale deed No. 5517 which was also executed by her by putting thumb impression. Except the deed of plaintiff all other deeds of transfer executed by Nur Khatun putting her thumb impression. But the plaintiff could not satisfy the court why at her old age she executed the deed in favour of plaintiff. Shamsul Alam by putting her signature who is an illiterate women. It is also submitted that after execution and registration of the sale deed in favour of defendant No. 1 on 05.04.1999, Nur Khatun handed over all her original deeds to the defendant No.1 which were submitted before the trial court and duly marked as exhibits. As such, the story of stealing the original documents from the house of plaintiff is false and fabricated and the diary lodged by him is only for the purpose of filing the instant suit.

15. Mr. Karim further submits that in the deed of the plaintiff there is no boundary at all specifying the property purchased by him and without specification of the suit property a decree declaring title cannot be passed on a vague schedule.

16. Finally, he submits that there is no misreading or non-consideration of any evidence by both the courts below. The trial court though wrongly held that the AC (Land) after passing order allowing mutation of the plaintiff has become functus officio and it cannot subsequently cancelled the order itself, the appellate court while disallowing the appeal rightly held that the AC (Land) has authority to review or to modify and to cancel the order passed by him if anything contrary comes before it. As such, both the courts below did not commit any error of law occasioning failure of justice.

17. Heard the learned Advocates for the parties, have gone through the revisional application, plaint, written statement, evidences both oral and documentary available in the lower court records and judgment and decree of both the courts below.

18. Admittedly, the property in question originally belonged to Nur Khatun by purchase. It is also not disputed that Nur Khatun by deed No. 2733 dated 11.06.1982 and deed No. 3008 dated 22.02.1983 (exhibits- and transferred part of the property to defendant No. 1. The said exhibits in original show that Nur Khatun in the year 1982 and 1983 executed both the deeds by putting her thumb impression. Moreover, said Nur Khatun while creating a charge over her property by mortgage to Sarea Khatun executed the mortgage deed on 10.12.1969 (exhibit-5) by putting her thumb impression and the deed No. 5517 dated 17.03.1982 executed by her in favour of one Md. Badruddin Biswas also executed by putting thumb impression, filed by the opposite party No. 1 by a supplementary affidavit dated 29.07.1999 which is admitted by P.W. 2.

19. The plaintiff claims that Nur Khatun executed a bainanama in his favour on 02.03.1998 for selling the property in question. Following said bainanama, Nur Khatun executed a sale deed on 09.03.1999 and registered the same on 23.06.1999 in favour of the plaintiff which is earlier than the deed of the defendant No. 1. As per provision of section 47 of the Registration Act, the sale deed takes effect from date of execution not from the date of registration and on that count the deed of the plaintiff is earlier one than the deed of the defendant No. 1. On the other hand the defendant No. 1's definite case is that the bainanama and sale deed of the plaintiff are forged and fabricated on the ground that Nur Khatun is an illiterate village women who earlier transferred her non-suited property to defendant No. I and one Badruddin and also mortgaged some of his property to Saera Khatun by putting her thumb impression and she cannot sign her name and never put any signature on any deed in the earlier. The plaintiff in suit could not bring any evidence contrary to the statement made by the defendant No.1 as well as contrary to the document submitted by the defendant No. 1 before the trial court. It would have been easier for the plaintiff to prove his case if he could produce Nur Khatun before the court who used to live with him in a same mess. But the plaintiff utterly failed to produce Nur Khatun before the court to support her written statement and the deed by which the plaintiff claims title in the suit property.

20. It is also found that the plaintiff did not cite and examine any attesting witness to the deed before the trial court to prove his case. Only the plaintiff deposed before the court to prove his deed and another witness, deed writer, while deposing as PW-3, in his cross examination could not satisfy the court in whose name the stamp was purchased.

21. I have gone through the plaintiff's bainapatra (exhibit 11) and sale deed (exhibit-8). It appears that Nur Khatun executed those documents by putting her signature which apparently, differs from each other. The stamp in question purchased in the name of one Ziaul Haque of chunati, Lohagora. The plaintiff is a man of Sitakunda and while deposing before the court he stated that he does not know said Ziaul Hauqe in whose name the stamp was purchased.

22. Moreover, stamp ought to have been purchased either in the name of purchaser or in the name of the vendor. In the instant case said Ziaul Haque in whose name the stamp was purchased also not an attesting witness to the deed. The plaintiff as purchaser ought to have known the person in whose name the stamp was purchased.

<u>23. In the absence of any conclusive evidence on the part of the plaintiff and non-examination of any attesting witness to the deed under challenge it cannot be construed that the deed was executed by Nur Khatun in his favour. Had Nur Khatun executed and registered the sale deed in favour of plaintiff she ought to have deposed before the trial court, in support of her written statement but for the reason best known to the plaintiff Nur Khatun was not examined. It is true that, to prove a deed of sale duly executed by the vendor an attesting witness is sufficient and there is no need of examining the vendor to prove a sale deed. But in the instant case the plaintiff did not even examined a single attesting witness to the deed. All those circumstances amply established that the deed by which the plaintiff is claiming title in the property has not been proved in accordance with law. Rather it establishes that Nur Khatun never put any signature on any document, but she executed all the documents earlier by putting her thumb impression. As such, both the courts below rightly found that the deed in question has not been proved.</u>

<u>24. The evidence produced both oral and documentary before the trial court by defendant No. 1 are sufficient to prove that the deed of the defendant No. 1 is genuine. As such, the suit is not at all required to be sent on remand to the appellate court or to the trial court for recording evidence of Nur Khatun which will not serve any purpose of the parties to the suit. It is to be noted that the plaintiff even could not satisfy the court what has prompted Nur Khatun to execute a deed at her old age by putting signature where she earlier executed as many as four deeds by putting her thumb impression and also could not satisfy that the plaintiff was delivered with the possession by specifying the property claimed by him.</u>

25. I have gone through the judgment and decree passed by both the courts below. It appears that the trial court while dismissing the suit exhaustively discussed all the evidences both oral and documentary and finally, came to a conclusion that the deed by which the plaintiff claiming title in the property is not a genuine deed and the said deed has not been proved in accordance with law. The appellate court also concurrently found that the plaintiff failed to prove his case and the documents submitted before the court claiming title by purchase from Nur Khatun.

In the absence of any cogent evidence in support of execution of the sale deed by Nur Khatun in favour of the plaintiff both the courts below rightly dismissed the suit as well as disallowed the appeal, and as such, I find no error in the decision occasioning any failure of justice.

26. Taking into consideration the above, this Court finds no merit in the Rule as well as in the submissions of the learned Advocates for the petitioner.

27. In the result, the Rule is discharged, however, without any order as to costs.

28. The order of status quo granted at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

29. Communicate a copy of this judgment to the court concerned and send down the lower court records at once.

End.

Mr. Farid Ahmed, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr Md. Ziaur Rahman, Advocate-On-Record.   ------- For the Respondent No.1 (In both the petitions). 
Respondent Nos.2-25 (In both the petitions) ---- Not represented

Mst. Shakhina Bewa wife of Abdul Gafur Miah. ------ Petitioner. (In both the petitions).

Abdul Hakim Siddique son of late Abdus Sattar Siddique and others. ------ Respondents (In both the Petitions)
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 24.08.2017 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3266 of 2012 heard along with Civil Revision No. 3278 of 2012).
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. These 02(two) civil petitions for leave to appeal are directed against the judgment and order dated 24.08.2017, passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division, in Civil Revision No. 3266 of 2012 heard along with Civil Revision No. 3278 of 2012 making both the Rules absolute upon setting aside the judgment and decree dated 10.06.2012, passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Court, Tangail, in Other Class Appeal No. 73 of 2011 heard along with Miscellaneous Appeal No. 26 of 2011 allowing both the appeals and reversing those dated 27.3.201] passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Ghatail, Tangail in Other Class Suit No. 76 of 2000 heard along with Pre-emption Case No. 43 of 2000 decreeing the suit and allowing pre-emption over the suit land.

<u>2. Since in both these two civil petitions the parties are same and the dispute also relates to the same land, thus both the petitions are taken up together and disposed of on the facts and circumstances shortly narrated below:</u>

<u>3. That, the present respondent No.1 instituted Other Suit No. 76 of 2000 and also filed Pre-emption Case No. 43 of 2000 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Ghatail, Tangail, one for declaration that the alleged Ewaznama deed No. 483 dated 18.1.2000 executed by defendant No.2 in favour of defendant No.1 and registered with the Office of the Sub Registrar, Ghatail, Tangail, is actually a deed of sale and the other one for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act of the self same property, respectively. It is stated that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 without disclosing anything to the plaintiff/petitioner, very secretly created a deed of exchange dated 18.1.2000 showing TK. 17,000/- as the value of the suit land and got the same registered in the Sub Registry Office. Thereafter, the defendant No.2 sold .34 acre of land from the schedule of the said exchange deed to defendant No.1 by a so-called sale deed dated 23.5.2000 at a consideration of taka 10,5000/- for the same, meaning that the defendant No.1 got back the same by the said so-called sale deed. In fact, there was no transaction of consideration money and no handing over of possession of the land in question. The price of both the exchanged and sold land always remained the same. It is stated that the plaintiff came to know about the aforesaid two deeds on 15.7.2000 when the defendant No.2 went to hand over possession of the land in question to defendant No.1 and thereafter, on 26.7.2000 upon obtaining the certified copy of the alleged deed. Thus he instituted the suit.</u>

4. In the pre-emption petition the present respondent No.1 stated that the case land measuring .67 acre, along with other lands in plot Nos. 88, 86 and 87 of Mouza-Bhadrabari, PS. Ghatail, Tangail, originally belonged to Abdul Gani Siddique and his wife, Somedonnessa. That on the death of Abdul Gani Siddique his wife Somedonnessa became the owner and possessor of the aforesaid land. Her two sons, namely, Abdus Sattar and Abdul Majid having died earlier, Somedonnessa distributed her entire properties between her living sons, daughter and grandson and granddaughter by a registered wasiatnama dated 7.4.1960 pursuant to which her son Abdul Latif, Monir Uddin, daughter Rowshanara, grandson (the plaintiff/pre-emptor) and his other brother and sister got their saham in the suit property. Defendant Opposite Party No.2 and his brother (sons of predeceased Abdul Majid) became the owners and possessor of the suit land by dint of Hiba Bil Ewaz from Somedonnessa. The daughters of predeceased Abdus Sattar gifted their saham to the plaintiff respondent No.1 herein and also to defendant opposite party Nos. 2 and 3. In this way, the plain-tiff/petitioner became the co-sharer tenant in the case jote by way of inheritance; that the defendants/opposite parties having full knowledge about the same created the so called ewaz (exchange) deed dated 18.1.2000 in order to frustrate the right of pre-emption of the plaintiff and as such, the plaintiff/pre-emptor(respondent No.1, of both the civil petitions), instituted the suit for declaration to the effect that the deed of exchange dated 18.1.2000 is actually a deed of sale and therefore, he has a right of pre-emption of .67 acre of land which was transferred by the said so called deed of exchange dated 18.1.2000 to defendant No.1 by defendant No.2.

5. Defendant No.1 who is also pre-emptee opposite party No.1 contested the suit as well as the pre-emption case by filing written statement and written objection denying all material averments made in the plaint as well as in the application for pre-emption. Her contention inter alia is that admittedly the suit land along with other lands belonged to Abdul Gani Siddique and his wife Somedonnessa and it is also admitted that their two sons, Abdus Sattar and Abdul Majid died earlier. The defendant although admits the wasiatnama dated 7.4.1960 executed by Somedonnessa after the death of her husband Abdul Gani Siddique, but she claims that the plaintiff, who is son of late Abdus Sattar, one of the predeceased sons of Abdul Gani Siddique, did not get any property by the said wasiatnama and as such he is not a co-sharer tenant in the case jote by inheritance because Abdus Sattar died earlier to the owners of the jote. It is contended that admittedly Abdul Gani Siddique died leaving behind Somedunnessa, his wife, 2 sons and one daughter to inherit the properties left behind by him. Monir Hossain and Abdul Latif, two living sons of Somedonnessa, transferred the suit land along with other lands to Mojibar Rahman, who, then sold the same to his wife Mahmuda by a deed of sale. Mofizur Rahman, son of Majibar Rahman and Mahmuda gifted .47 acre of land and .20 acre of land respectively to the defendant No.2 by two gift deeds both dated 30.01.1995. The suit land described in the first schedule to the plaint measuring .67 acre of land was not fertile land, there was a homestead in plot No.88. That by earth filling all the lands of suit Plot Nos. 86, 87 and 88 have been developed. The land of Plot No. 116 is fertile land. The value of both the lands being the same the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, for the purpose of smooth cultivation, executed and registered the ewaz deed dated 18.1.2000 and thereafter on 19.1.2000 the defendant No.2 took possession and started cultivating paddy through bargadar. The said defendant also upon taking possession of .67 acre of land of Plot No.88 filled up .32 acre of land by earth and constructed house thereon and is possessing .34 acre of land of Plot No. 86 to 87 by cultivation. Thereafter, the defendant No.2 sold .34 acre of land of Plot No. 116 to defendant No.1 by registered deed of sale dated 23.5.2000. In this way, the defendant No.1 became the owner and possessor of 1.01 acres of land by the aforesaid two deeds. Since the alleged deed is a deed of exchange the plaintiff petitioner has no right to pre-empt the same and as such both the cases should be dismissed.

6. The trial Court heard both the cases analogously and framed as many as six issues for determination of both the cases including: (1) Whether the alleged Ewaz deed is liable to be decreed as deed of sale? (2) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to pre-empt the suit land? (3) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to the relief as prayed for?

7. The trial Court upon hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record decreed the suit on contest against defendant No.1 and ex parte against rest of the defendants upon declaring that the deed of exchange dated 18.1.2000 is actually a deed of sale not a deed of exchange and thereby allowed the pre-emption case over the case land against the pre-emptee opposite party No.1 on contest and ex parte against the rest by a single judgment and decree and judgment and order respectively dated 27.3.2011.

8. Being aggrieved by the same, the defendant No.1, who is also pre-emptee No.1, preferred Title Appeal No. 73 of 2011 and Miscellaneous Appeal No. 26 of 2011 before the learned District Judge, Tangail which were eventually heard by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Tangail who by his judgment and decree and judgment and order respectively dated 10.6.2012 allowed both the appeals and reversed the judgment and decree and judgment and order respectively of the trial Court. Thus the plaintiff/pre-emptor moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos. 3266 of 2012 and 3278 of 2012 respectively and obtained Rule and stay.

9. A Single Bench of the High Court Division heard both the Rules together and ultimately, by a single judgment and order dated 24.8.2017 made both the Rules absolute and reversed the judgment and decree and judgment and order of the lower appellate Court and restored the judgment and decree and judgment and order of the trial Court. Hence these two civil petitions have been filed by the defendants/pre-emptee.

10. Mr. Probir Neogi, the learned senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner in both the civil petitions submits that the High Court Division erred in making the Rules absolute as it travelled beyond the scope of the revisional jurisdiction since the finding of fact, whether concurrent or not, arrived at by the appellate Court upon considering the evidence on record, are immune from interference under the revisional jurisdiction. He further submits that the appellate Court having regard to the meticulous consideration and elaborate discussions of the evidence on record passed the judgment upon reversing the findings of the trial Court, but the High Court Division while passing the impugned judgment held that 'the deed in question is an out and out sale deed not a deed of exchange on the ground that one of the exchanged property was bought back and/or on the ground of difference of price of the land of exchanged deed and the subsequent deed of sale' which is misconception of law because by oral evidence proving of document is excluded under section 91 of the Evidence Act.

11. Mr. Farid Ahmed, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.1 in both the civil petitions submits that the plaintiff/pre-emptor-respondent No.1 is the co-sharer tenant in the suit jote by inheritance, but the defendant No. 2, in order to frustrate his right of pre-emption, created the deed of exchange which is actually a deed of sale as found by the trial Court as well as by the High Court Division and as such, the High Court Division did not commit any illegality in passing the impugned judgment which is based on proper appreciation of the facts and law and as such, the same is liable to be affirmed by this Division.

12. On hearing the learned Senior Advocates of both the sides and on penisal of the materials on record, including the judgments of all the Courts it appears that admittedly the suit land along with other lands belonged to Abdul Gani Siddique and his wife Somedonnessa, whose names were recorded in SA Khatian Nos. 94, 97 and 99(Exhibits 1/Kha Series). After the death of Abdul Gani, his wife Somedonnessa became the owner and possessor of the entire property. Her two sons Abdus Sattar and Abdul Majid died long before and as such Somedonnessa distributed her entire properties amongst the living sons, daughter, grandson and granddaughter through her deceased sons, by registered wasiatnama No. 425 dated 7.4.1960 (Exhibit No.2). The plaintiff/pre-emptor (respondent No.1 in both the civil petitions) claims that in view of the aforesaid wasiatnama and by inheritance he is a co-sharer tenant in the case jote. It is claimed that daughters of late Abdus Sattar also gifted their saham, which they got from the case jote by way of the said wasiatnama, to the plaintiff. Accordingly the plaintiff/pre-emptor claimed that in order to frustrate his right of pre-emption the defendants created the said exchange deed which is actually out and out a sale deed.

13. On the other hand, the defendant/pre-emptee (petitioner herein) although admits the execution and registration of the said wasiatnama but claimed that the plaintiff did not get any property by the said wasiatnama and as such he is not a co-sharer-tenant in the case jote. His further claim is that for the purpose of smooth cultivation of land he exchanged the lands with defendant No.2 and subsequently, 41:- the defendant No.1 by sale deed dated 23.5.2000 got .34 acre of land from the schedule No.2 of the exchange deed from the defendant No.2. However, the defendant did not produce the subsequent sale deed dated 23.5.2000 before the trial Court for dealing with the same in accordance with law.

14. The trial Court on perusal of the said wasiatnama (Exhibit-2) found that the executrix, Somedonnessa, mentioned in the body of the said wasiatnama that since her son Abdus Sattar died earlier, the son and daughter of Abdus Sattar (her grandson and granddaughter) would get .73 acre of land. Such statement has been proved by the corroborative evidence of P.Ws. 2, 3 and OPWs (DWs)-1 and 2 and as such, the trial Court held "the plaintiff appears to be a co-sharer tenant in the case jote by inheritance". It further held "the Ewaz Deed dated 18.1.2000 is an out and out a sale deed". Relying upon the principle laid down in the case of Shafi Than Vs. Mannujan Hossain wife of A.Z.M. Delwar Hossain, Advocate and others reported in 35 DLR (AD) 226 and also in the case of Alfazuddin Mollah and others Vs. Md. Almas Chokder and another reported in 56 DLR (AD) 179 and considering the evidence of O.P.Ws (D.Ws). 1 to 3 the trial Court thus held that "the plaintiff is entitled to get pre-emption over the case land as a co sharer-tenant in the case jote and the alleged deed of ewaz is actually a deed of sale".

15. The lower appellate Court, on the other hand, though concurred with the findings of the trial Court to the effect that the plaintiff is a co-sharer-tenant in the case jote but it held that 'the pre-emption application of the applicant is not allow-able because the alleged deed dated 18.1.2000 is an ewaz deed against which no pre-emption case can be filed'. It further held that 'since the ewaz deed has been registered its contents cannot be varied on the basis of the oral evidence'. In this respect it relied on the case of Joynal Abedin Mollah Vs. Aliar Rahman and others reported in 3 BLDOD)105 and accordingly allowed both the appeals and set aside the judgment and decree and judgment and order passed by the trial Court and thereby dismissed the suit as well as the pre-emption case.

16. In revision, the High Court Division on perusal of the evidence of OPW (D.W).1 and the deed of exchange dated 18.1.2000, found that 'the price/value of .67 acre of exchanged land has been shown as TK.17,000/- only in the exchange deed but the price of the land mentioned in the sale deed dated 23.5.2000 has been shown at TK.10,500/- for only .34 acre of land. Thus the price in the sale deed dated 23.5.2000 has apparently been shown at a decreased price than that of the earlier price of the exchange deed although the sale deed has been registered later. Therefore, the High Court Division held that 'the sale deed dated 23.5.2000, in the name of Most. Sakhina Bewa, defendant No.1/pre-emptee (present petitioner), executed by Md. Monsur Rahman Siddique defendant No.2/pre-emptee No.2, is nothing but a deed created only for the purpose of returning back the property received by the earlier deed of exchange. Thus it held that 'the price as has been mentioned in the sale deed is not the actual value/price of the land in question rather that has been show/mentioned, with ill motive which is not the actual price of the land in question. Therefore, such ewaz has been created with the ill motive to frustrate the right of the pre-emptor to pre-empt the sale and as such the same is liable to be interfered with by the Court of law. The High Court Division also held that in the aforementioned back drop the deed of ewaz dated 18.1.2000 (Exhibit 3-Ga) does not fall within the legal and lawful objective of an ewaz deed, rather it clearly appears to have been made with an illegal intention to defeat the statutory right of the pre-emptor.

17. The High Court Division accordingly held that 'the decision reported in 3 BLD 1983(AD) 105, on the basis of which the appellate Court allowed the appeal and thereby dismissed the suit would not be applicable in the case in hand'. In respect of sections 91 and 92 of the Evidence Act the High Court Division relied on the decisions reported in PLD 1960 (Lahore) 231 and AIR 1936 (PC) 70 and held "section 92 does not preclude a party from showing that the writing was not really the contract between the parties, but it was only a fictitious or colourable device which cloaked something else. In such situation of a particular case, oral evidence is admissible to show that the document was only a sham or nominal transaction and was not intended to be acted upon or to show that the written document for conveyance of property was only a fictitious exchange to defeat and infringe the statutory right of other'. It further held that 'when a document is meant merely on a informal memorandum of transaction and not as a document embodying disposition of property, oral evidence is not excluded'. It further appears that the High Court Division also relied upon the case reported in AIR 1958(SC)448 and held "Section 92 of the Evidence Act is not a bar to leading oral evidence to prove that the document in question is not an exchange deed but actually a sale deed." It further held "admission of oral evidence of the acts and conducts of the parties in determining the true nature of the transaction does not infringe provision of section 92 of the Evidence Act. If it can be shown by oral evidence that though the document in particular form was executed but in fact it is different from what it appears to be." Thus the High Court Division made the Rule absolute.

18. Considering all these aspects and the decisions reported in AIR 1958(SC) 15, wherein it has been held "extrinsic evidence to determine the effect of an instrument is permissible where there remains a doubt as to its true meaning," the High Court Division rightly held "there is no bar in sections 91 and 92 of the Evidence Act to adduce parol evidence to show notwithstanding the recital of exchange not to it's true perspective nature and object in a document".

19. On perusal of all the judgments, it appears that the lower appellate Court being the last Court of fact on perusal and consideration of the materials on record concurred with the finding of the trial Court that 'the plaintiff is a co-sharer ten-ant in the case jote' but even then it allowed both the appeals holding that “নালিশী দলিলটি যেহেতু এওয়াজ দলিল হিসেবে সম্পাদনপূর্বক রেজিষ্ট্রি হয়েছে মর্মে দেখা যায় সেহেতু মৌলিক সাক্ষ্য দ্বারা উক্ত দলিলের contents পরিবর্তন করা যাইবে না” He came to such finding relying on the decision reported in 3BLD(AD) 105. But such finding is totally erroneous pursuant to a subsequent decision of this Division in the case of Alfazuddin Mollah and others Vs. Md. Almas Chokder and another (56 DLR(AD)179) wherein in paragraph 10 this Division observed "In this case it has been specifically alleged that in order to defeat the pre-emption the deed in question has been shown as deed of exchange but actually the transaction was a sale thus we are of the view that when the nature of transaction becomes doubtful on the specific allegation being made out by the appellate pre-emptor then for the interest of justice matter is required to be tested by adducing evidence in the trial Court in order to ascertain the nature of transaction and to decide the case properly by way of interpreting the document in question." The facts and circumstances of the afore-mentioned case and those of the case in hand being identical the principle laid down therein has binding effect.

<u>20. Moreover, the plaintiff having proved his case by adducing sufficient evidence and more specifically when the defendant/pre-emptee admits the wasiatnama there is no reason to disbelieve the fact that the plaintiff is a co-sharer tenant in the case jote and both the Courts of fact have rightly found the same. Thus within the span of 4(four) months time after the so-called exchange deed when defendant No.2 transferred half of the exchanged land to defendant No.1 at a lesser price, the exchange deed proves to be a sham transaction executed with ill motive of frustrating the plaintiff/pre-emptors statutory right of pre-emption.</u>

21. Thus, the findings and decision arrived at by the High Court Division being based on proper appreciation of fact and law the same does not call for any interference by this Division.

22. Accordingly, both the civil petitions are dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.
