VS
Dr. ATM Gulam Kabir and others ---------- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
In this Civil Revision, the Rule was issued calling upon opposite party Nos.1-10 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 11-11-2010 (decree signed on 21-12-2010) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Noakhali in Title Appeal No.84 of 2000, affirming the judgment and decree dated 15-3-2000 (decree signed on 27-3-2000) passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Noakhali in Title Suit No.53 of 1984, decreeing the suit should not be set-aside and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper, shall not be passed.
Pending the hearing of the Rule, the operation of the judgment and decree dated 11-11-2010 passed in the said Title Appeal No.84 of 2000 was stayed initially for 6(six) months. The period of stay was subsequently extended from time to time.
2. One Robindra Kumar Ghosh as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.53 of 1984 in the Court of learned Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Noakhali for a declaration that the Kabala Deed Nos.21203, 21204, 21205, and 21206 all were executed on 6-10-1978 and registered on 7-10-1978 purportedly executed by Robindra Kumar Ghosh in favour of Mst. Ozifa Khatun is forged, fraudulent, without any consideration, false, collusive, ineffective, and not binding upon the plaintiff as well as upon the suit property.
3. The plaintiff's case, in short, is that the original plaintiff Robindra Kumar Ghosh got some properties from his father Deb Chandra Ghosh by a registered deed of gift dated 10-4-1976. Then, he sold 2.18 acres of land to the defendant Nos.2-8 by different sale deeds. While Robindra Kumar Ghosh and defendant Nos.2-8 were in possession of their respective land, they came to know that having falsely personated a man as Robindra Kumar Ghosh got 4(four) kabala deeds registered bearing Nos. 21203, 21204, 21205 and 21206 all dated 7-10-1978 in favour of defendant No.1. But Robindra Kumar Ghosh never executed such sale deeds. He did not know about it and those kabala deeds were created by forgery. He did not put any thumb impression or signature in any such deed, nor did he execute and register the same upon appearing in person before the Sub-Registrar but, defendant No.1 got the said forged deed executed and registered by falsely personating any of her man as Robindra Kumar Ghosh. Even, he did not receive any consideration from defendant No. 1. Thus, defendant No.1 was never in possession of the suit land. At that time, Robindra Kumar Ghosh had no necessity for selling or intention to sell the suit property. But the unruly sons of defendant No.1 being greedy for others' properties created those forged documents in favour of their mother, defendant No.1. Initially, Robindra Kumar Ghosh came to know about the said forged deeds at the last part of the month of Chaitra, 1390 BS and exactly he came to know about the same on 24-4-1984 and 25.04.1984 and upon obtaining certified copy thereof and, as such, that very Robindra Kumar Ghosh as plaintiff instituted the suit.
4. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations brought by the plaintiff and contending, inter alia, that in the need of cash, Robindra Kumar Ghosh proposed to sell the suit property and the defendants accepted the proposal. Upon negotiation, the consideration money was fixed at Taka 72,000. Accordingly, four deeds all dated 6-10-1978 were executed by Robindra Kumar Ghosh upon receiving the entire consideration money in the presence of the witnesses and the same were registered on 7-10-1978 while one Shafiullah identified him before the Sub-Registrar. Thus, all four deeds are genuine and those were executed and registered upon receiving the consideration money by Robindra Kumar Ghosh himself. Accordingly, he also made delivery of possession except for a part of his homestead wherein he had been living with the promise that he would go elsewhere. But Robindra Kumar Ghosh subsequently might have created several deeds in favour of defendant Nos.2-8. But he never disclosed the same to defendant No.1 while defendant Nos. 2-8 are not in possession in any part of the suit land. Thus, the said deeds have not been acted upon. It is not true that the four sons of defendant No.1, Mostafa Miah, Golap Rahman, Shahjahan and Nazim Uddin created the forged deed. Accordingly, the plaintiff filed the false suit only to cause damage to defendant No. 1. Thus, the plaintiff having no right, title or possession of the suit property, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
5. During the trial, the plaintiff was twice examined by an Advocate Commissioner appointed by the Trial Court on 11-12-1985 as the suit was taken up for hearing ex-parte and then, on 8-7-1986 when the matter was subsequently taken up for hearing on contest. But the defendants did not cross-examine him. Then, he on 4-8-1986 executed six kabala deeds in favour of AKM Golam Kabir and others in respect of 5.70 acres of land and accordingly made delivery of possession thereof. But before registration of the said six kabala deeds, he suddenly died on 7-8-1986. Thereafter, his wife Promila Sundari submitted an application for substitution. During the pendency of the said application for substitution, their two sons, Profulla Kumar Ghosh and Monilal Ghose came from India with Indian passports and having appeared before the Sub-Registrar, they identified the execution of the said six kabala deeds by their father Robindra Kumar Ghosh. Accordingly, all those six deeds were registered on 4-11-1986. In those deeds, Promila Sundari, wife of Rabindra Kumar Ghosh and other men of his homestead were witnesses. Subsequently, Promila Sundari separately and their two sons, Profulla Kumar Ghosh and Manilal Ghose filed a joint application before the Trial Court that AKM Golam Kabir and others, the purchaser of the suit land from their father should be considered as the assignees of their father Robindra Kumar Ghosh.
6. Upon a contesting hearing, the said applications were allowed. Accordingly, AKM Golam Kabir and others were made assignees of Robindra Kumar Ghosh. Thus, they were superimposed as plaintiffs.
7. During the trial, the plaintiffs examined 11(eleven) witnesses and exhibited some documents, which were marked as exhibits 1-7. On the other hand, the defendants examined 5(five) witnesses and produced only the certified copies of four kabala deeds.
8. Upon hearing both the parties, the learned trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 15-3-2000 (decree signed on 27-3-2000) decreed the suit.
9. Against the judgment and decree of the Trial Court, defendant Nos.1(ka)-1(uma) preferred Title Appeal No.84 of 2000 before the Court of the learned District Judge, Noakhali and the appeal was transferred to the 2nd Court of Additional District Judge, Noakhali for its disposal. The Court of Appeal below upon hearing both the parties by the judgment and decree dated 11-11-2010 (decree signed on 21-12-2010) dismissed the appeal.
10. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the Court of Appeal below, defendant No.1(ka) only as petitioner filed the instant Civil Revision and obtained the Rule and the interim order of stay.
11. Having placed the Civil Revision, Mr Shasti Sarker along with Mr Md Abdur Rashid, learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that both the Courts below failed to consider that upon execution and registration of the deeds in question, the plaintiff himself delivered the possession of the suit property and they have still been in possession and thus, the sale deeds have been acted upon. Both the Courts below also failed to consider that the subsequent purchasers had no legal right and authority to continue the suit on behalf of the sole deceased plaintiff. Again, both the Courts below failed to consider that the thumb impressions and signatures of the deceased plaintiff as appeared in the volume book were not compared with those in the admitted documents. Moreover, neither the thumb impression expert nor the handwriting expert properly conducted their respective examination and therefore, the reports submitted and the opinion made by them being not in accordance with the law, the suit should be sent on remand for trial afresh specially, for examination of the thumb impression and signatures of the original plaintiff as appeared in the volume books by comparing the same with any admitted thumb impressions or signatures of that very deceased plaintiff the learned Advocate further submits that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner as therein it has not been prayed for setting aside the sale deeds in question as required by section 39 of the Specific Relief Act.
12. On the other hand, Mr Abul Kalam Chowdhury, learned Advocate for opposite party Nos.l-5 and 7-10 submits that both the Courts below concurrently found that the kabala deeds in question are forged documents upon considering the report as well as the depositions of the thumb impression expert and the handwriting expert. Against the application for sending five registered deeds executed by the original plaintiff for comparing the thumb impressions and signatures of the original plaintiff therein with the purported thumb impressions and signatures of the original plaintiff that appeared in the respective volume books, defendant No.1 or her heirs did not raise any objection and in the written objection against the report of the handwriting expert, they have also not raised any objection as to the admitted thumb impressions and the signatures of the original plaintiff and in the written objection against the report of the thumb impression expert, they stated in a contradictory way, once stating that those were not properly compared then, said that those were not even admitted thumb impression but, the said objections were rejected. Against the said rejection, the defendants did not take any step, nor even had they taken any ground in the Memo of Appeal and thus, they have conceded the said order of rejection. Accordingly, both the Courts below rightly made their findings and observations on the said reports and depositions of the thumb impression expert and the handwriting expert. The opposite parties who are the purchasers of the suit property were made assignees of the original plaintiff as they got six sale deeds executed in their favour and then all those deeds were registered upon identification of thumb impression and signatures therein by his two sons inasmuch as in all such deeds, the wife of the original plaintiff and his neighbouring people in the same homestead were also witnesses to the execution of the said six sale deeds. Against the order allowing the applications for appointment of assignees of the original plaintiff though, the defendants filed a written objection, they were not aggrieved by the order passed by the Trial Court. Accordingly, the purchaser plaintiffs were continuing the suit without any subsequent objection as well as based on the order of the learned Trial Court. Moreover, since admittedly the subsequent plaintiffs are the purchasers of the suit land from the original plaintiff thereby, their right, title and interest were created by those sale deeds and as per law, during the lifetime of the original plaintiff, they were entitled to be assignees of the original plaintiff as per Order XXII, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure and accordingly, there being no merit in the Rule, the same should be discharged with cost. The learned Advocate further submits that since both the Courts below concurrently found that the four kabala deeds in question are forged documents but, they have used the same as genuine before the Courts below as well as before this Court, a proceeding should be drawn against them under section 476 read with section 195 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
13. I have perused the Civil Revision application along with the records of the Courts below and heard the learned Advocates from both sides.
14. As per the plaintiffs' case, Robindra Kumar Ghosh never executed and registered any sale deed in favour of the original defendant No.1 nor even, he received any consideration money from her and accordingly, he also did not make the delivery of possession of the suit property. On the other hand, it is the case of the original defendant No.1 that Robindra Kumar Ghosh himself executed all four deeds and got the same registered upon appearing before the concerned Sub-Registrar and in furtherance thereof, he also made delivery of possession of the suit property upon receiving the consideration money hi the presence of the witnesses.
15. Admittedly, Robindra Kumar Ghosh himself as the plaintiff instituted the suit. Even, during his lifetime he was examined by the Court through the Advocate Commissioner on two occasions once when the suit was taken up for an ex-parte hearing and then when the suit was taken up for the contesting hearing. It appears from the record that an Advocate Commissioner was appointed subsequently in the presence of the learned Advocate for defendant No.1 upon serving notice on him. But defendant No.1 did not cross-examine him. Therefore, his deposition before the Advocate Commissioner stillremains uncontroverted nor even shaken. Promila Sundari Ghose, wife of Robindra Kumar Ghosh also was examined, and she was cross-examined on behalf of defendant No. 1. They could not bring out anything from her inconsistent with the deposition of Robindra Kumar Ghosh. Moreover, for the fairness of justice, Robindra Kumar Ghosh himself submitted an application before the Trial Court on 2-1-1986 for comparison and examination of the thumb impressions and signatures that appeared in the respective volume books with his admitted signatures put in some earlier sale deeds. Then, the assignee plaintiffs also filed similar applications and upon hearing both the said applications, the same was allowed by the Trial Court. Against those applications, defendant No.1 or her heirs even did not file any written objection alleging that those are not admitted deeds of sale purportedly executed by Robindra Kumar Ghosh. Accordingly, five registered deeds, one of which was even executed and registered before the purported execution and registration of the defendants' deed of purchase.
The thumb impression expert and the handwriting expert submitted their separate report with the findings and observations that the thumb impressions and the signatures purported to be those of Robindra Kumar Ghosh as appeared in the respective volume books are different from those that appeared in the five sale deeds executed by Robindra Kumar Ghosh.
16. During the hearing, the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners submits that to properly examine the thumb impressions and signatures, the respective expert ought to have been compared them along with all 18 points and thus, those examinations and the reports made thereon were not properly and legally done. In the case of the State of Madhya Pradesh vs Sita Ram Gajraj Sing Rajput, 1978 MPLJ 197 (200) corresponding to 1978 CrLJ 1220 it was heldthat no hard and fast rule can be laid down for fixing the number of points of similarities. Even each case has to be seen on its own merits and in case of any well-grouped characteristics in a narrow area and pattern uncommon, six points or even less may be sufficient to fix the identity.
17. In another case report in AIR 1978 SC 1183, it was held that a comparison of 8 points of similarity is sufficient to conclude. But if two prints agree in the pattern configuration of redesign the pattern area and also agree in three or more ridge characteristics regarding shape and location, it can be safely said that the two points are identical to each other.
18. Similarly, Mr F. Brewester feels satisfied that clear six points of identity would be enough for concluding identity when two points are sufficient to conclude no identity of given prints with the admitted prints. Therefore, to conclude the no identity of the given prints with the admitted prints dissimilarity at two points is sufficient.
19. In the present case, it appears from both reports that the respective experts came to their conclusion upon examining at least five points. Thus, I do not find any legal infirmity in examining the thumb impressions and signatures of Rabindra Kumar Ghosh by the thumb impression expert as well as by the handwriting expert. Accordingly, upon considering the deposition of Robindra Kumar Ghosh and those of other witnesses including the handwriting expert and thumb impression expert, both the Courts below concurrently held that the sale deeds purportedly executed and registered by Robindra Kumar Ghosh in favour of the original defendant No.1 who was substituted by her four sons and one daughter are forged documents.
20. Even, it is admitted by the defendant-petitioner that Robindra Kumar Ghosh and his family were in possession of the homestead within the suit properties and the remaining suit properties beyond the homestead are cultivable land. Having meticulously considered the depositions about the possession, both the Courts below concurrently found that the plaintiffs have been able to prove their possession therein. Even at this stage, the learned Advocate for the petitioners could not show any misreading of any material evidence on record. It appears that both parties adduced their evidence in support of their possession but upon proper assessment, it also appears that both the Courts below rightly came to their findings on possession in their respective judgments.
21. It also appears that the original defendant No.1 died leaving behind four sons and one daughter and they were substituted in the Trial Court. They have also jointly preferred the appeal but only the petitioner alone filed the instant Civil Revision. Thus, from the conduct of other appellants, it appears that they have conceded the judgment and decree of the Courts below. Had there been any merit in their case, they might have filed the instant Civil Revision along with the sole petitioner. Thus, even the circumstantial evidence does not support that the defendant-appellant-petitioner is alone in the possession of the suit property.
<u>22. It is a long-established principle of law that when a purported executant alleged the purportedly executed deed as a forged one, he cannot be treated as a party to the forged deed and accordingly, there is no legal necessity for cancellation of the forged deed or document and mere prayer for declaration that those are forged, fraudulent and not binding upon the purported executant is sufficient. In this regard, the case of Sufia Khanam Chowdhury vs Faizun Nesa Chowdhury, 39 DLR (AD) 46 and the case of Awlad Hossain and others vs Ebadulla Dewan and others, 12 BLC (AD) 148 may be relied on. In the last case, some forged documents were the subject matter, and it was only prayed for a declaration that those are forged, fraudulent, fabricated and not binding upon the plaintiffs. The Trial Court decreed the suit. The Appellate Court allowed the appeal while the High Court Division sent the case on remand enabling the plaintiff to amend the plaint by inserting a prayer for cancellation of the forged deed. On appeal, the Appeal Division set-aside the judgment and decree of the High Court Division and thereby upheld the judgment and decree of the Trial Court. The similar facts and law involved in the case in hand. Accordingly, the principle laid down in the case reported in 12 BLC (AD) 148 is squarely applicable to the case at hand.</u>
23. In such view of the matter, I do not find any merit in the Rule.
<u>24. It is the specific case of the plaintiff that four sons of defendant No.1 created the disputed sale deeds by forging the thumb impressions and signatures of the original plaintiff and upon trial both the Courts below concurrently found substance in the case of the plaintiff. Upon considering the material evidence on record, I have also no hesitation to conclude that the original defendant No.1 and her heirs are the beneficiaries of those forged documents and, as such, they themselves in collusion with each other have or caused to have created and registered those sale deeds by forging the signatures and thumb impressions of Robindra Kumar Ghosh upon falsely personating him with intent to cause damage and injury to the original plaintiff as well as his successors-in-interest, to support a title in the suit property, to cause the original plaintiff or his successor-in-interest to part with the suit property and thereby have made valuable securities in respect of the suit property, and fraudulently possessed and used the same as genuine documents as well as corruptly used as true or genuine evidence in this suit before all three Courts, including this Court and thereby prima facie have committed offences under section 93/196/205/463/465/467/471/474/109 of the Penal Code, 1860.</u>
25. Therefore, I find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the opposite parties that the trial Court should be directed to draw a proceeding under section 476 read with sections 195(1)(b)(c) and 195(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure against the substituted defendants as well as the present petitioner.
26. Accordingly, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.
<u>27. However, the Trial Court is hereby directed to file a complaint as per section 476 read with section 195(1)(b)(c) and (3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 against the substituted defendants as well as the present petitioner and their accomplices if any, for committing offences described in the preceding paragraph in the Court of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Noakhali within 30(thirty) days from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.</u>
Send down the records of the Courts below immediately.
End.

full_judgment:
Kashefa Hussain, J: Supplementary-affidavit filed by the petitioner do form part of the main petition. 

2. Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why cancellation of allotment of the land measuring 3(three) Katha situated at Plot No. 5, Road No. 4, Sector-15/C-1, Uttara (3rd Phase) Extension Project Residential Area, Uttara, Dhaka which has been transferred to the petitioner by the lessee by way of a registered deed with due approval from the respondent No. 2 and confiscating the money deposited against the said land vide Memo No. RAJUK/ESTATE and Land-2/UTTARA/562 Stha; dated 9-3-2020 issued by the respondent No. 6 (Annexure-P to the writ petition) and all subsequent steps/actions taken by the respondent No. 2 pursuant thereto and the threat of the respondent No. 6 made on 29-9-2021 to evict the petitioner from aforementioned Plot No. 5 should not be declared to have been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

3. The petitioner Tania Rahman, wife of Md Mujibur Rahman of House No. 5, Road No. 3, Block-B, Dumni, Pink City, Khilkhet. Dhaka is a citizen of Bangladesh. 

4. The respondent No. 1 is the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works, Building No. 5, Bangladesh Secretariat, Dhaka-1000, the respondent No. 2 Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (RAJUK), represented by its Chairman, the respondent No. 3 is the Liason Officer, Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (RAJUK), the respondent No. 4 is the Senior System Analyst. "9. No persons, who has already been allotted a plot for residential purpose, in his/her name or in the name of his/her, wife/husband or in the name of dependent children or any other dependent, by the Trust or the Government in any Housing Estate or by the Board of Revenue of any khas land or any person who has already a house within the jurisdiction of Dhaka and Narayanganj Municipal Committee or suburb of these Municipal areas within the jurisdiction of the Trust, shall be allotted a plot. All applicants shall have to file an affidavit to be signed by a 1st class Magistrate to the effect that neither he nor any one of his dependents as specified above possesses any residential plots within the aforesaid jurisdiction. 
10. Any application received with false shall be summarily rejected. In case, an allotment is made to any one on the basis of false information in the application and the information is subsequently found incorrect, the allotment shall stand cancelled.”

Placing his reliance on clause 9 and 10 of the Dhaka Improvement Trust (Allotment of Lands) Rules 1969, he echoes the submissions of the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 2. He argued that clause 9 and 10 of the Dhaka Improvement Trust (Allotment of Lands) Rules 1969 clearly presupposes that in the face of any discovery of suppression of fact the plot shall stand automatically cancelled. He also echoes the submission of the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 2 that since the Dhaka Improvement Trust (Allotment of Lands) Rules 1969 significantly state that the plot shall stand cancelled, he persuades that the language of the clause 9 and 10 of the Dhaka Improvement Trust (Allotment of Lands) Rules, 1969 do not presuppose any prior notice and therefore no notice is necessary to he served by the term of the lease-deed whatsoever. 

24. Next he submits that the petitioner has no locus solidi to file the writ petition since the cancellation of plot was made against the original lessee and not in the name of the petitioner. He concludes his submission upon assertion that the Rule bear no merits ought to be discharged for ends of justice. 

25. We have heard the learned Counsels, perused the application and materials before us. Evidently the respondent No. 2 cancelled the plot in question which was originally allotted in the name of the respondent No. 8 who is the original lessee. Admittedly the respondent No. 2 pursuant to allotment in the name of the original lessee in 2011 after exhausting necessary procedures also executed lease-deed in 2012 in the name of the present lessee the petitioner here. It is an admitted fact that subsequently the respondent No. 8 with the clear permission of the respondent No. 2 transferred the plot in the name of the petitioner. Several documents have been annexed in the writ petition in support of the transfer in the name of the petitioner by the respondent No. 8 with clear permission of the respondent No. 2. We have particularly drawn our attention to annexure LI of the writ petition wherein the respondents upon allowing the plot to be transferred in the name of the petitioner by its letter dated 22-8-2013 issued by the office of the respondent No. 2 inter (ilia clearly stated এখন হইতে আপনাকে উক্ত প্লটের হস্তান্তর সূত্রে লীজ গ্রহিতা/গ্রহিত্রী হিসাবে গণ্য করা হইবে. Therefore it is clear that the respondents while granting permission to transfer the plot in the name of the petitioner also acknowledged the petitioner as a lessee in the said plot. The respondents upon a query from this bench could not deny that the petitioner is not a lessee in the said plot. 

26. Sitting in writ jurisdiction it is primarily our duty to monitor as to whether any fundamental right of any person has been violated and it is also our duty to monitor as to whether due process has been served upon concerned person. 

27. While examining the relevant law of the land we drew our attention to the Dhaka Improvement Trust (Allotment of Lands) Rules, 1969. For our purpose we have particularly drawn attention to clause 9 and 10 of the Dhaka Improvement Trust (Allotment of Lands) Rules, 1969. Whoever or whatever might be done subsequently by any person which also include the respondents, nevertheless the statutory rules cannot be derogated or deviated from. The crux and principle of clause 9 and 10 of the Dhaka Improvement Trust (Allotment of Lands) Rules, 1969 is that any person who has been allotted any plot by the RAJUK, Government etc. cannot apply for a second allot presupposes that if such fact of being allotted a second plot is revealed or discovered by the RAJUK at any stage the second allotment shall stand cancelled. The learned Advocate for the respondents submitted that since the RAJUK clearly mandate that the second allotment shall stand cancelled on the basis of false information whatsoever, therefore there is no necessity to issue any notice. 

28. Against this submission of the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 2, we are of the considered view that even if the Dhaka Improvement Trust (Allotment of Lands) Rules, 1969 does not directly presuppose a notice but however principles of natural justice demand that a notice must be given to a person and no person shall be condemned until he has been given a chance to explain himself. In this case before us the respondent No. 2 contends that since the plot was allotted in the name of the original lessee therefore there is no need to serve any notice upon the petitioner. The respondents however argued that although no notice needs to be served upon the petitioner since she is not the original lessee, but however the respondents on several dates asked the petitioner to appear before them and accordingly the petitioner appeared before the respondents and which is manifest by way of হাজিরা which is annexure-Z-2 of the affidavit-in-opposition. 

29. We have perused the writ petition wherein the petitioner admitted that she was present by way of হাজিরা. The petitioner contended that since no reason for her appearance was stated in the said the notice therefore such notice cannot be treated as a proper show cause notice in the eye of law. 

30. Our considered view is that although the reasons are not cited directly in the notice but however it may be presumed that the petitioner was aware of the reason calling for her to appear before the respondents. 

31. However as mentioned above our duty here presently is to supervise as to whether there has been any violation of any primary right of any person particularly the petitioner here. Since admittedly by way of Annexure-L 1 the respondent acknowledged the petitioner as a fresh lessee therefore we are of the considered view that the parties are mutually duty bound to each other by way of the lease-deed which is Annexure-F of the writ petition. Since the respondents have acknowledged the petitioner as a lessee therefore both the parties are legally duty bound to each other to abide by the terms of the lease-deed. In the event of violation of the terms of the lease-deed by any party the other party is bound to answer the reason of the said violation. 

32. With this principle in mind we have drawn our attention to clause 26, clause 29 and clause 30 of the lease-deed. Clause 26 of the lease-deed presupposes that in the event of false statement or suppression of facts etc. including other circumstances the lessor shall be entitled to cancel the allotment to determine the provisions of the lease in accordance with clause 29 of the lease-deed. Such being the express intention of clause 26 of the lease-deed we have next drawn ourselves to clause 29 of the lease-deed. Clause 29 among other factors clearly contemplate the procedure on giving one calendar month's notice in writing to the lessee. Clause 30(iv) of the lease-deed also presupposes the circumstances under which a lease may be finally rejected and the circumstances are clearly described therein. 

33. For proper adjudication of this matter as to whether due process was given to the instant petitioner or not we have to mainly confine ourselves to the provision of service of notice as intended under clause 29(i) of the lease-deed read with clause 26 of the lease Deed. As mentioned above the respondent No. 2 could not deny that the petitioner stepped into the shoes of the lessee albeit with all the duties and liability of the previous lessee by virtue of being the new lessee. As discussed elsewhere in this judgment the Dhaka Improvement Trust (Allotment of Lands) Rules, 1969 must be complied with. However since admittedly the respondents particularly by way of Annexure-LI clearly acknowledge the petitioner as the new lessee of the allotted plot therefore the terms of the lease-deed must be abided by both parties. In this particular case however it is clear that the provisions of clause 29 read with clause 26 was not followed by the respondents. Therefore we are of further considered view that in accordance with the principles of natural justice no person should be condemned unheard. In this particular case we are relying upon the terms of the lease-deed. We are of the opinion that the respondents owe a duty to afford due process to the petitioner since she is admittedly a fresh lessee in the allotted plot. 

34. Under the facts and circumstances and the foregoing discussions made above and after hearing the submissions of the learned Advocate for both sides we are inclined to dispose of the Ride with the above observations. 

35. In the result, the Rule is disposed of. The cancellation of allotment of the land measuring 3(three) Katha situated at Plot No. 5, Road No. 4, Sector-15/C-1, Uttara (3rd Phase) Extension Project Residential Area, Uttara. Dhaka which has been transferred to the petitioner by the lessee by way of a registered deed with due approval from the respondent No. 2 and confiscating the money deposited against the said land vide Memo No. RAJUK/ ESTATE and Land-2/UTTARAI562 Stha; dated 9-3-2020 issued by the respondent No. 6 (Annexure-‘P' to the writ petition) is hereby set-aside. 

36. The respondents are at liberty to issue a notice under clause 29(1) of the terms of the lease-deed Annexure-L-1 read with clause 26 if they are advised and dispose of the matter in accordance with the Dhaka Improvement Trust (Allotment of Lands) Rules, 1969 including any other Rules that may be applicable in the instant case. 

The order of status-quo granted earlier by this court is hereby vacated. 

Communicate this judgment at once. 

End.

Md. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate with Abdul Barek Chowdhury, Advocate—For the Petitioners. 
Abdur Rahman, Advocate—For the Opposite Party Nos. 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 & 9. 
Md. Khalilur Rahman (Helal) with Mintu Kumar Mondal, Advocates—For the Opposite Party Nos.73-101.

Baby and others  -------- Plaintiff-Appellant-Petitioners

full_judgment:
At the instance of the petitioners, the Rule was issued by this Court with the following terms: 
"Records be called for. Let a Rule be issued calling upon the opposite party Nos.1-12 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 4-1-2021 (decree being drawn on 11-1-2021) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 377 of 2012 disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 29-8-2012 (decree being drawn on 2-9-2012) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 114 of 2010 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

2. Facts leading to the issuance of the Rule are, inter alia, that the petitioners and the opposite party Nos. 70-71 filed Title Suit No. 05 of 1993 in the 4th Court of the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka for partition of the suit property stating, inter alma, that the suit property originally belonged to Maghu Chowkider and his name was correctly recorded in CS Khatian. Thereafter, Meghu Chowkider died leaving behind two sons, namely-Sheikh Yeasin and Kalimuddin. The property appertaining to schedule Nos. 4 and 5 of the plaint belonged to Sheikh Yeasin. Sheikh Yeasin died in the year 1946 leaving 3 sons, namely-Momtazuddin, Sultan and Magrab Ali, 3 daughters, namely Sharifunnessa, Uttam Nessa and Joytunnessa who possessed the property left by Sheikh Yeasin in ejmali. Thereafter, Momtazuddin died in the year 1968 leaving behind one son, namely Abdul Awal, wife Moti Bibi and 5 daughters Anwara, Fulbanu, Afatunnessa, Sademunnessa and Saleha Khatun. Abdul Awal died in the year 1970 leaving behind mother Moti Bibi, wife Shamsunnahar, 3 sons Montu, Reazuddin and Jashimuddin and 4 daughters Farida, Arjuda, Parul and Kuna. Magrab Ali also died in the year 1962 leaving behind wife Dona Bibi, 3 sons, namely Abdul Matin, Salahuddin and Chand Miah and 4 daughters, namely Nazia Khatun, Razia Khatun, Hamida Khatun and Sufia Khatun. Kalimuddin transferred his share to Salimuddin by way of gift. Salimuddin died in the year 1974 leaving behind wife Talemunnessa, 2 sons, namely Nasir Uddin and Abdul Majid and 7 daughters, namely Akter Banu, Nur Banu, Pari Banu, Angura, Hosne Bibi, Shamsunrkahar, Nurunnahar, Abdul Karim and Abdur Rahim. Thereafter, Abdur Rahim died in the year 1965 leaving behind wife Kadbanu, two sons, namely Zaman Mollah and Hasan Mollah and four daughters, namely Madina, Kulsum, Nazma, Hanufa. Abdul Karim died in the year 1970 leaving behind wife Mabia, and 4 sons, namely Mohsin, Shafiullah, Md. Anis and Md. Yunus. The defendant Nos. 23-45 inherited 11 annas share of Salimuddin. Joytunnssa and the daughter of Yeasin died leaving behind 3 sons, namely Ramizuddin, Rafizuddin, Tafizuddin and 3 daughters, namely Falani, Rahimon, Anna Bibi and Debjan Bibi inherited from Joytunnessa. The defendant Nos. 52-67 are reported to have purchased a portion of the said property and, as such, they have been made as party. The plaintiffs are the successive heirs of the 3 daughters of Sheikh Yeasin and they are entitled to get 1 anna 15 gonda 2 kara 2/3 kranti share from the property. The plaintiffs have been possessing the property by way of ejmali share. The plaintiffs requested the defendants for partition of their shares, but the defendants did not agree with the prayer of the plaintiffs and, as such, they filed the suit for partition of the suit property against the defendants. 

3. The defendant Nos. 15-18, 19 and 72 appeared in the suit and contested the same by filing written statements contending inter alia that the suit was barred by limitation as well as had for defect of parties. The suit land belonged to CS recorded tenant Meghu Chowkider who died leaving behind two sons, namely Sheikh Yeasin and Kalimuddin who possessed the same. Sheikh Yeasin during his lifetime transferred his share in favour of his son Magrab Ali by way of heba-bil-ewaj executed on 22-10-1945 and registered on 23-11-1945 being deed No. 4252 and delivered possession of the same. Sheikh Yeasin also transferred some property in favour of his two sons, namely Momtazuddin and Sheikh Sultan by registered heba deed executed on 22-10-1945 and registered on 23-11-1945 being deed No. 4252. Yeasin Sheikh also transferred his property in favour of 2 sons by way of heba and delivered the possession in their favour. In the aforesaid way, the three sons of Sheikh Yeasin became the owners of the property. After transfer, Sheikh Yeasin remained owner of some property. After death of Yeasin Sheikh, they made an amicable partition amongst themselves and as per the said amicable partition, Magrab Ali got 09 decimals of land from Plot No. 621, an area of 151/2 decimals of land from Plot No. 746, an area of 101/2 decimals of land from Plot No. 747. Magrab Ali died leaving behind wife Dona Bibi; the defendant No. 15, three sons and four daughters; the defendant Nos. 16-22 and the defendant Nos. 16-18 purchased the share of the four sisters by a registered kabala deed dated 5-1-1984 being deed No. 527. Dona Bibi also transferred her 2 annas share in favour of the defendant Nos. 16-18 by way of oral gift on 15-3-1978. Sheikh Yeasin while possessing his remaining share gave his daughters cash money, gold ornaments, cattle heads in their saham and, as such, the three daughters of Sheikh Yeasin did not inherit immovable property of Sheikh Yeasin. 

4. The defendant Nos. 15-18, 19, 68-71 and 73 contested the suit by filing a written statement stating, inter alia, that the Meghu Chowkider was the original owner of the suit property and died leaving behind 2 sons, namely Sheikh Yeasin and Kalimuddin. They claimed to have purchased 29 decimals of land from the suit land from the heirs of 3 sons of Magrab Ali by the registered deeds dated 4-10-1978 and 6-11-1978 from the suit plot No. 1433. At the time of the trial, the plaintiffs examined two witnesses, namely Sanaullah (PW1) and Md. Siraj Miah (PW2). The defendant Nos. 15-18 and 72-73 examined three witnesses including the defendant No. 16 on behalf of the defendant Nos. 68-71 and 73 and the defendant No. 68 himself and they were cross-examined by the plaintiff. After conclusion of the trial, the Trial Court dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 25-11-1999. 

5. Impugning the judgment and decree of the Trial Court, the plaintiffs preferred First Appeal No. 156 of 2000 before the High Court Division. After hearing, the High Court Division was pleased to allow the appeal and accordingly sent back the suit on remand with a direction to dispose of the original Suit as per the observation made in the body of the judgment. After hearing the parties, the Trial Court dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 19-4-2012. 

6. Challenging the legality and propriety of the judgment and decree of the Trial Court, the plaintiffs again preferred Title Appeal No. 377 of 2012 before the Court of the learned District Judge, Dhaka. After admitting the appeal and observing all other formalities, the learned District Judge was pleased to transmit the record to the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Dhaka for disposal. Upon hearing, the learned Additional District Judge was pleased to dismiss the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 4-1-2021. Being aggrieved by and highly dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the plaintiff-petitioners moved this Court and obtained the aforesaid Rule and status quo thereto. 

7. Mr. Md. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Senior Advocate along with Mr. Abdul Barek Chowdhury appearing on behalf of the petitioners took me through pleadings and evidence on record and also the judgment of the Courts below and submits that the Trial Court miserably failed to appreciate the observation as set forth in the judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal (F.A) No. 156 of 2000 and most illegally dismissed the suit. The Appellate Court without its independent assessment of evidence on record and direction made in the aforesaid FA No. 156 of 2000 simply dittoed the judgment of the Trial Court and, as such, committed an error of law causing a serious failure of justice, therefore, the same is liable to be turned down to secure the ends of justice. He further submits that the defendants failed to prove the Exhibits- Kha, Ga, and Uma i.e. the alleged deeds of heba-bil-ewaz in respect of passing of consideration. DW-1 Abdul Matin in his deposition did not state that he was present at the time of passing consideration nor he stated that the alleged deeds of heba-bil-ewaz were registered in his presence, moreover, the DW-2 was not an attesting witness of the alleged deeds and in cross-examination, he stated that there was no witness at the time of passing of consideration though the defendant No. 3 stated that he himself along with his three brothers and witness Abed Ali (PW-1) were present at the time of passing of consideration but DW-1 did not corroborate the statement of the DW-3 as the DW-1 neither stated that he was present at the time of passing consideration nor stated that DW-2 Md. Rafiq along with his brothers were present. Therefore, it is crystal clear from their evidence that they failed to corroborate each other in respect of passing of consideration. The High Court Division found those contradiction and accordingly, passed the judgment in the earlier First Appeal with the direction to deliver the judgment afresh giving findings to the effect that the defendants failed to prove that Sheik Yeasin transferred the property by heba-bil-ewaz deed as well as oral deed during his life time but the Trial Court as well as the Appellate Court failed to appreciate the finding of the High Court Division and passed the impugned judgment and decree and, as such, committed an error of law resulting in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further submits that no attesting witnesses were examined, therefore, it can be safely concluded that the impugned deeds are ex facie illegal as no consideration was passed. 

8. In support of his submissions, the learned Advocate for the petitioners has referred to the decision reported in 7 BLD (1987) (AD) 306 and 2 BLC (AD) 85. He next submits that the heba-bil-ewaz is equivalent to a sale deed and in transaction of heba-bil-ewaz, consideration must be passed, undoubtedly, the adequacy of consideration is not the question. A consideration must be perfectly valid which is wholly inadequate in amount when compared with the thing given, if a gift of ring may be a sufficient consideration but it must be actually and bonafidely paid to the doner. He further adds that in the instant case, the jaynamaz and the Holy Quran are consideration against the heba-bil-ewaz but the defendants have failed to prove that the jaynamaz and the Holy Quran as consideration are actually given to the executor of the deeds, moreover, where there has been no payment of the ewaz; the document cannot be ewaz and invalid in the eye of law but both the Courts below failed to understand the intent of the law. In this respect, he has referred to the case of Ranee Khujooroonissa, Widow of Enayut Hossein Jehan reported in the Law Reports (Indian Appeals) the Privy Council Vol. III, 1875-6 and in another case of Monowara Begum and another vs Rupban Bibi and another reported in 23 BLC 444. He further submits that the concurrent findings of the Courts below are not immune from any interference since the judgments of the Courts below suffer from misreading or non-consideration of evidence. In this respect, he has referred to the decision reported in 73 DLR (AD) 250 and 40 DLR (AD) 62. 

9. Per contra, Mr. Abdur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 and 9 submits that the learned trial Court after considering the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record the trial Court rightly dismissed the suit and the appellate court by its independent and dispassionate consideration of evidence on record concurred with the decision of the trial Court, therefore, the concurrent finding is immune from any interference by this Court and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. Mr. Rahman further submits that on the basis of the heba and oral gift the record of right has been prepared in the name of the defendants and, as such, the plaintiffs lost their co-shareship in the suit land, as such, the suit for partition is not maintainable, therefore, the courts below rightly dismissed the suit and, as such, no interference is called for by this court. 

10. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman (Helal), the learned Advocate with Mr. Mintu Kumar Mondal appearing for the opposite party Nos.73-109 submits that both the Courts below correctly found that Sheikh Yeasin was the predecessor of the plaintiffs and contesting defendants gifted the suit land to his three sons by means of three heba-bil-ewaz deeds and his three daughters got ornaments and cattle heads and, as such, after the sad demise of Sheikh Yeasin, the three daughters did not claim their shares before filing the present suit and therefore, there is no apparent reason to interfere with the concurrent finding of the facts as there is no misreading, non-consideration of evidence and non-interpretation of law critically involved in this case. In this respect, he has referred to the case reported in 15 BLD (AD) 82. He further submits that the opposite party Nos. 73-101 claimed their title through Kalim Uddin and not Sheikh Yeasin and the plaintiffs claimed their portion of land from Sheikh Yeasin and, as such, the suit is decreed and they are entitled to get saham of 0.1323 acre of land since the predecessor of the added opposite parties Abdul Latif was not made party and the observation is required to be given in the judgment. In this connection, the predecessor of the added opposite party Nos. 73-101 became the owners of 0.15 acre of land by way of purchase as well as exchange in the year, 1990-94 and accordingly, separate city survey khatian being No. 5685/1 was duly prepared and published in his name but the plaintiff filed the suit without impleading him as defendant and, as such, the suit is bad for defect of party. 

11. In this respect, he has referred to the decision reported in 37 DLR (AD) 268. He further submits that the added opposite party No. 73-101 along with 17 others purchased 0.1323 acre of land vide registered sale deed No. 2798 dated 6-9-2020 from aforesaid Abdul Latif and started construction work after getting plan from the RAJUK on 16-2-2021. But due to the order of status quo dated 5-9-2021 passed by this Court, the construction work has been stopped and, as such, he filed an application for permission to continue their construction work. After modifying the order of status quo dated 5-9-2021, it was kept with the record to be considered at the time of hearing the Rule and accordingly, an observation is required to be made since the land of the added opposite parties are distinctive and different from the land claimed by the plaintiff as it has been settled that no order of injunction is passed stopping the construction work in urban area. 

12. Heard the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates of the parties and perused the entire materials on record with care and attention and seriousness as they deserve. The convoluted question of law critically embroiled in this case has meticulously been waded through. 

13. Now the pertinent question is whether the impugned judgment is sustainable in the eye of law. 

14. The Trial Court dismissed the suit holding the view that the suit is not maintainable as the plaintiff did not claim any relief against the impugned three registered heba-bil-ewaz deeds dated 23-11-1945 are genuine and the contentions of the oral gifts are proved. He further held that the oral gifts and the three registered heba-bil-ewaz deeds were acted upon as the latest khatian was prepared in the name of the defendant. The Appellate Court concurred with the judgment and decree of the Trial Court and held that on the basis of the judgment passed in First Appeal No. 156 of 2000, the Trial Court started the trial again and wherein one Momota Rani Chackrovorty was examined as DW-5 who brought the volumes of the registered heba-bil-ewaz deeds and held that the judgment and decree of the Trial Court are based on sound reasoning. In this respect, the relevant portion of the judgment of the Appellate Court may be read as follows: 
"উপরোক্ত আরজী, জবাব এবং সাক্ষ্য প্রমাণগুলি পর্যালোচনা করলে দেখা যায় যে, নালিশী তফসিলভুক্ত সম্পত্তির মূল মালিক ছিলেন মেগু চৌকিদার এবং উক্ত মেগু চৌকিদারের মৃত্যুতে ইয়াসিন ও কলিমউদ্দিনের ২ পুত্র স্বত্ব দখলকার হন। কলিমউদ্দিন মারা গেলে তার ১ পুত্র সলিমউদ্দিন ওয়ারিশ হিসেবে স্বত্ব দখলকার হন। অন্যদিকে ইয়াসিন মারা গেলে তার ৩ কন্যা উত্তমনেছা, শরীফুন নেছা ও জয়তুন্নেছা ওয়ারিশ বিদ্যমান থাকেন। এই তথ্যগুলি বাদী এবং প্রতিদ্বন্ধিতাকারী বিবাদীপক্ষ প্রত্যেকে স্বীকার করেন। কাজেই এই তথ্যগুলিকে সত্য বলে ধরা নেয়া যায়। প্রতিদ্বন্ধিতাকারী বিবাদীগণ দাবী করেন যে, ইয়াসিন তার জীবদ্দশায় তার স্বত্ব দখলীয় সম্পত্তি তার ৩ পুত্রের মধ্যে মৌখিক ও দানপত্র দলিলমূলে ভাগ-বাটোয়ারা করে দেন। অন্যদিকে তাদের হিস্যার পরিবর্তে নগদ অর্থ, স্বর্নালংকার এবং অন্যান্য মূল্যবান উপহার সামগ্রী প্রদান করেন। বাদীপক্ষ উক্ত বিষয়ে অস্বীকার করে। তবে পি ডব্লিউ-১ সাক্ষ্য প্রদান করেই স্বীকার করেন যে, তিনি হেবা বিল এওয়াজ দলিলগুলির বিষয় মামলার আগে থেকেই জানতেন। অন্যদিকে মৌখিক ও দালিলিক দানপত্র বিষয়ে বিবাদীপক্ষে দালিলিক ও মৌখিক সাক্ষ্য প্রমাণ দাখিল করা হয়েছে যা বাদীপক্ষ তাদের জেরায় খান করতে সক্ষম হন নাই। অত্র মামলার নথি পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, মামলাটিতে প্রথমে ২৫-১১-৯৯ ইং তারিখের একটি রায় প্রচার করা হয়েছিল। উক্ত রায়ে মামলাটি পক্ষদোষে এবং সকল সম্পত্তি হচপটে না আনায় ত্রুটির কারণ উল্লেখ করা হয়। এ বিষয়ে পরবর্তীতে উক্ত রায়টিকে চ্যালেঞ্জ করা হলে মহামান্য সুপ্রীম কোর্ট এফ এ নং ১৫৬/২০০০ মোকদ্দমায় ২৮-৭-০৮ইং তারিখে একটি বিস্তারিত পর্যবেক্ষণ তুলে ধরেন। উক্ত পর্যবেক্ষণে বলা হয যে, হেবাবিল এওয়াজ দলিলগুলি সঠিক রয়েছে কি না সে বিষয়টি বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালতের সাক্ষ্য প্রমাণ গ্রহণের মাধ্যমে নির্ধারণ করার সুযোগ থাকা সত্ত্বেও বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত উক্ত বিষয়ে পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ করে নাই। এছাড়াও মূল মোকদ্দমার বিভিন্ন তারিখের আদেশে পক্ষদোষ এবং হচপটের বিষয়ে একাধিক আদেশ এর উল্লেখ করে মহামান্য আদালত উল্লেখ করেন যে, মামলাটির সকল পক্ষকে সুযোগ দিয়ে পুনরায় আরজী ও জবাব সংশোধনের মাধ্যমে সাক্ষ্য প্রমাণ গ্রহণের মাধ্যমে নিষ্পত্তি করা হলে ন্যায় বিচার নিশ্চিত হবে। ফলে মামলাটি Send back করা হয় এবং পুনঃবিচারে কার্যক্রম চালু করা হয়। নথি দৃষ্টে দেখা যায় যে, পুনঃ বিচারকালীন সময়ে বাদী এবং প্রতিদ্বন্ধিতাকারী বিবাদীপক্ষকে একাধিকবার আরজী ও জবাব সংশোধনের আবেদন মঞ্জুর করা হয় এবং নালিশী তফসিলসহ পক্ষদের নাম সংশোধন করা হয়। ফলে নথি দৃষ্টে দেখা যায় যে, অত্র মামলাটিতে কোন পক্ষদোষ বা হচপট দোষ বা রক্ষণীয়তার বিষয়ে কোন বিতর্ক হওয়ার কোন কারণ নাই। বিগত ২৯-৮-১২ ইং তারিখের রায়টি পর্যালোচনা করলে দেখা যায় যে, উক্ত রায়ে হেবা বিল এওয়াজ দলিলগুলির বিষয়ে এবং মৌখিক সাক্ষ্য প্রমাণ বিষয়ে বিস্তারিত আলোচনা করা হয়েছে। উক্ত রায়ে পক্ষদের মধ্যে বিতর্কিত ইস্যুগুলিকে বিস্তারিত আলোচনা করেই সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ করা হয়েছে। অত্র আদালতও উক্ত সাক্ষ্য প্রমাণগুলি পর্যালোচনায় একই রকম তথ্য পায়। এছাড়া আপীল আদালতে নুরুদ্দিন এর সাক্ষ্য গ্রহণ করা হয়। উক্ত নুরুদ্দিন আর.ডব্লিউ-১ হিসেবে সাক্ষ্য প্রদানকালে বলেন যে, নালিশ জমি মহানগর জরীপে তাদের নামে রেকর্ডকৃত হয়। উক্ত আর. ডব্লিউ-১ এর জেরা হতে বিতর্কিত কোন তথ্য পাওয়া যায় না।"

15. The execution of the heba-bil-ewaz deeds have not been denied by the plaintiff. It is well settled that a registered deed shall presume to be genuine and the person who says it is ingenuine has to prove to that effect. The deeds are of more than 68 years old and at the relevant time of recording evidence, the deed was 54 years old. The plaintiff side did not put forward any suggestion to the DW-1 that no ewaz or consideration was passed. DW-2 Abed Ali aged 80 deposed that Yeasin transferred the suit land to his three sons but the plaintiff side did not make any suggestion as to whether his sons handed over a copy of the Holy Quran and the jainamaz. It is the cardinal principle of law of evidence that oral evidence cannot be admissible against the documentary evidence except few exceptions as laid down under section 92 under provisos 1-6 of the Evidence Act. In this respect, the relevant portion of the section 92 of the Evidence Act may be read as follows: 
"When the terms of any such contract, grant or other disposition of property or any matter required by law to be reduced to the form of a document, have been proved according to the last section, no evidence of any oral agreement or statement shall be admitted, as between the parties to any such instrument or their representatives in interest, for the purpose of contradicting, varying, adding to, or subtracting from, its terms; Proviso (1). Any fact may be proved which would invalidate any document, or which would entitle any person to any decree or order relating thereto; such as fraud, intimidation, illegality, want of due execution, want of capacity in any contracting party, want or failure of consideration, or mistake in fact or law. 
(2) ………………..
(3) ………………..
(4) ………………..
(5) ………………..
(6) ………………..

16. The burden of proof to invalidate a document lies upon the plaintiff. Moreover, on the basis of the registered deed, SA and R.S khatians were prepared in the names of the defendants. No two case are similar, every case has to be considered with its own facts and circumstances. The contentions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner is that in the instant case, the Holy Quran and the jainamaz are the consideration against the heba-bil-ewaz but it was not given to the executor of the deeds. The executor of the deeds in his life time did not say anything as to that effect that he was not given consideration i.e. the Holy Quran and the jainamaz. Since the executions of the deeds in question were not disputed, therefore, it is not essential to produce attesting witness. If the execution of a registered deed is denied by the executant then the same may be proved by an attesting witness or by producing the scribe of the deed in question or the person who knows the hand writing of the execution or by comparison of the disputed signatures with the admitted one and thumb impression or by producing thirty years old documents from a proper custody. 

17. On perusal of the recital of impugned deeds, it appears that the executant transferred the land as mentioned in the three heba-bil-ewaz deeds upon receiving the Holy Quran and the jainamaz, therefore, it cannot be held that the aforesaid deeds were not genuine and the Courts below considering the facts and circumstances of the case rightly held that the aforesaid three deeds are genuine but the Courts below wrongly held that the rest of the property of Yeasin was transferred by the oral gift. To be a valid oral gift under the Muslim Law, there must be an offer, acceptance and delivery of possession. The defendants by adducing cogent and reliable evidence hopelessly failed to prove the story of the oral gift that Yeasin transferred his rest of the land to his aforesaid three sons. The contention of the defendants is that the three heba-bil-ewaz deeds were registered on 23-11-1945 and the oral gift was made on 31-12-1945. It is preposterous to believe on the facts and circumstances of the case that after one month of registered heba-bil-ewaz deed, Yeasin transferred the rest of his property depriving his three daughters but the Courts below without any valid reason accepted the contention of the oral gift made by Yeasin. The DW-1 in his evidence stated that in lieu of the property, Yeasin paid money, ornaments and cattle heads to his three daughters but it is not supported by any evidence. The Courts below failed to consider that being daughters of Sheikh Yeasin, they have every right to inherit the properties of their father. Unless it is proved by cogent and reliable evidence that they gave up their claim to their right of inheritance or they were totally ousted by Sheikh Yeasin by legal means. The possession of the co-sharers cannot be adverse to other co-sharers is a well-established principle of law but the Courts below hopelessly failed to consider the same. In our society, it is common phenomenon that after marriage the female co-sharers live separately with their husbands' abodes and they exercise their right of possession through their brothers and others. The Trial Court wrongly held that since SA and RS records were not prepared in the names of the plaintiff-petitioners, they were not entitled to get any share from Sheikh Yeasin. The record of right does not confer any title and it will in no way disentitle the co-sharers to have their shares through the intervention of the Court. 

18. The opposite party Nos. 73-101 claimed their title through Kalimudddin; the full brother of Yeasin and therefore, they are entitled to get saham in respect of 0.1323 acre of land as successive purchaser and exchanged deed. The said land was duly recorded in the city survey; therefore, the defendant Nos. 73-101 may continue their construction work because the plaintiff-petitioners have got no right to interfere with the construction work started by the aforesaid defendants in the afore noted land admittedly belonged to Kalimuddin. 

19. The facts and circumstances of the instant case are quite distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the cases referred to by the learned Advocate for the petitioners. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, my penultimate conclusion is that the land belonging to the three heba bil ewaz deeds shall not be included in the saham of the three daughters of Sheikh Yeasin. In respect of the rest of the land, the sons shall be entitled to get saham in respect of 6/9 share and the daughters shall entitle to get saham in respect of 3/9 share. 

20. In the result, the Rule is made absolute in part. The impugned judgment and decree of the Court below is hereby set-aside in part. Accordingly, the Title Suit No. 1145 of 2010 (original Title Suit No. 129 of 1978) is decreed in part in preliminary form. The plaintiffs shall get '5/9 shares in respect of the suit land belonging to Sheikh Yeasin excluding the land apper-taining to registered heba-bil-ewaj deeds being Nos. 4250/1945, 4251/1945 and 4252/1945 (Exhibits-Ga, Gha, Uma). The parties are directed to effect partition amicably by metes and bounds within 60(sixty) days from the date of receipt of this judgment by the Trial Court failing which, the parties may get their shares on partition through the intervention of the court by appointing an Advocate Commissioner. The defendants may pray for their saham before the trial court after submitting requisite court fees, if so advised. The Advocate Commissioner shall consider the possession, convenience and inconvenience of the parties and value of the land in distributing the saham among the parties to the suit. The earlier order of status quo granted by this Court, thus, stands recalled and vacated. 

Let a copy of the judgment with LCRs be sent down to the Courts below at once. 

End.
